3.en:
**A decree.** See on ch. 1:1–4. The superficial differences between this copy of the decree and that recorded in ch. 1:1–4 are due to the fact that this copy was for official use only, whereas the other was published. The decree made public contained a permit to return to Palestine, to rebuild the Temple there, and to collect money for that purpose, but it made no mention of the decision of Cyrus to support the erection of the Temple with public funds (see on ch. 1:4). However, the copy of the decree that served as a directive for the officers of the realm clearly stated that the cost was to be met by the royal treasury (ch. 6:4). Exact specifications as to methods of construction were given in this copy.
The height thereof. The figure here given for the height of the new Temple is twice that of the Temple of Solomon, and its width three times as great (see 1 Kings 6:2). The length of the new structure is not given; that of Solomon’s Temple was 60 cu. Yet the new edifice is said to be “as nothing” in comparison with that of Solomon’s (Haggai 2:3), and those who had seen the Temple of Solomon wept they saw the foundation of the new building, because of the obvious inferiority of the latter (Ezra 3:12; cf. PK 564). It is not impossible that the length of the cubit measure of Cyrus’ decree differs somewhat from that of the Jews, though it is hardly possible that the difference should have been so great as to reconcile the apparent discrepancy between the facts noted. It is more reasonable to think that Cyrus gave permission for a much larger edifice than the Jews actually built. But with a royal subsidy (see on ch. 1:4) it is difficult to think that they would have been content with a structure so much inferior to that of Solomon. It may be that the dimensions given in Cyrus’ decree are for the front of the Temple only, which was of more magnificent proportions than the rest of the building.
3.zh:
古列王元年，他降旨論到耶路撒冷神的殿，要建造這殿為獻祭之處，堅立殿的根基。殿高六十肘，寬六十肘，

**降旨。**見拉1:1-4註釋。這個諭旨的副本和拉1:1-4的記錄之間所存在著表面的差異，是因為副本是官方內部使用的，而正本則是公佈於眾的。公開的諭旨裡包括准許迴歸巴勒斯坦，在那裡重建聖殿，為此而籌款，但沒有提到居魯士決定動用公共基金來幫助建造聖殿（見拉1:4註釋）。但諭旨的副本是用來指導帝國官員的，清楚地說明經費是由國庫來承擔的（拉6:4）。副本詳細規定了建築的方式。
**殿高。**這裡說的新殿高度是所羅門聖殿的兩倍，寬度是三倍（見王上6:2）。沒有說明新殿的長度。所羅門聖殿的長度是六十肘。可是與所羅門的聖殿相比，新殿據說是“如無有”（該2:3）。那些見過所羅門聖殿的人，看到新殿的根基時竟哭了，因為後者明顯不如前者（拉3:12；參《先知與君王》564頁）。居魯士諭旨裡的肘有可能與猶太人的肘有差異，但不可能大到像上面所說的那種程度。更有可能是猶太人所造的殿遠遠沒有達到居魯士所批准的那麼大。但他們既有王室的援助（見拉1:4註釋），很難理解他們怎麼會滿足於那遠不如所羅門聖殿的建築。也許居魯士的諭旨所描述的尺寸是比較輝煌的聖殿正面，而不是其餘部分。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–5節）**。《先知與君王》第558頁。

6.en:
**Tatnai.** Concerning Tatnai and the other men here mentioned, see on ch. 5:3, 6.
Be ye far from thence. It may be that the author of the official report incorporated in Ezra 6 has abbreviated or condensed the letter of Darius, and given only the essential parts of it—a résumé of the decree of Cyrus, and the confirming decree of Darius. The first important point of Darius’ letter is a warning to the officers of the satrapy “Beyond the River” against interfering with the work at Jerusalem. The language of the whole letter shows that a strong and determined king ruled the state. Some of the decrees of other Persian rulers, as recorded in Ezra and Esther, clearly reveal vacillation on the part of the issuing monarchs.
6.zh:
現在河西的總督達乃和示他波斯乃，並你們的同黨，就是住河西的亞法薩迦人，你們當遠離他們。

**達乃。**關於達乃等人，見拉5:3,6註釋。
**你們當遠離他們。**拉6章所記錄官方報告的作者可能簡縮了大流士信函的內容，只列出主要的內容：居魯士的諭旨和大流士進一步確認的諭旨。大流士諭旨最重要的一條是警告“河西”總督轄地的官員不要干預耶路撒冷的工程。這封信的整個語氣都顯示一位強有力的國王在統治著國家。其他波斯國王的一些諭旨，如記錄在《以斯拉記》和《以斯帖記》裡的，則表現出國王方面的搖擺性。

14.en:
**They prospered.** The Jews, who had experienced so many troubles and disappointments during recent years, could have expected no greater or more joyful surprise than the message of Darius’ new decree. Suddenly were fulfilled the prophecies of Haggai, who had reminded them that their God was the owner of silver and gold, and that it would be easy for Him to supply the necessary means to complete the task they had begun in faith (Haggai 2:8). On the day when the new foundation had been laid, the Lord had promised, “From this day will I bless you” (Haggai 2:19). Marvelous was the fulfillment. In fact, the blessings in view must have exceeded their most daring hopes.
The other prophet of those days had asked, “Who hath despised the day of small things” (Zech. 4:10)? How miserable and poor their efforts seemed to be when they began a second time to build the house of their God. Although they had obeyed the prophets, and had started to build, there was fear in their hearts. They were surrounded by enemies. However, they had trusted in the word of the prophet, who emphatically stated that “the hands of Zerubbabel,” which had “laid the foundation of this house,” should “also finish it,” and that in this way they would know that the Lord of hosts had sent him to them (Zech. 4:9).
Artaxerxes. Some older commentators who identified the Artaxerxes of ch. 4:7 as the false Smerdis, naturally identified Artaxerxes of ch. 6:14 also as the false Smerdis. But the king here mentioned is Artaxerxes I, and for two reasons: 1. It is hardly conceivable that Smerdis would have issued a favorable decree, after having been hostile—all within the 7 months of his reign. 2. Because the Artaxerxes here mentioned is listed in order after Darius. By the time of Ezra, Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes had all issued decrees regarding the Temple and its services. There appears to be a contradiction between the statement that Artaxerxes’ decree was required for the completion of the Temple and the statement in v. 15 that the Temple “was finished” during the reign of Darius. This apparent contradiction may be resolved on the reasonable assumption that Artaxerxes’ beautifying of the house of the Lord (ch. 7:27) was in a very real sense of the word a final finishing of the building of the Temple. Hence Ezra felt justified in including Artaxerxes as the third of three kings whose decrees made possible the restoration of the Temple and of Jerusalem (see chs. 7:27; 9:9).
Mention of the king Artaxerxes in this verse is evidence that the book of Ezra was written, not in the time of Zerubbabel, but in that of Ezra, probably during the reign of Artaxerxes.
14.zh:
猶大長老因先知哈該和易多的孫子撒迦利亞所說勸勉的話就建造這殿，凡事亨通。他們遵著以色列神的命令和波斯王古列、大利烏、亞達薛西的旨意，建造完畢。

**凡事亨通。**猶太人近年來遭遇許多困苦和失望。所以大流士新諭旨的消息給他們帶來了極大的歡樂。哈該的預言一下子應驗了。他曾提醒他們，上帝是金銀的主宰。祂很容易提供必要的資財，使他們完成所開始的工作（該2:8）。在立新根基的那一天，上帝承諾，“從今日起，我必賜福與你們”（該2:19）。這個承諾神奇地應驗了。事實上眼前的福氣一定超過了他們最大的期望。
當時的另一位先知問：“誰藐視這日的事為小呢”（亞4:10）？他們第二次開工建造聖殿的時候，他們的力量顯得那麼渺小和可憐。雖然他們聽從了先知的話開始建造，但他們心中懼怕，四面受敵。然而他們相信了先知的話語。先知強調說“所羅巴伯的手立了這殿的根基，他的手也必完成這工”。這樣，他們就知道乃是萬軍之耶和華派他到他們那裡的（亞4:9）。
**亞達薛西。**過去有些註釋家把拉4:7亞達薛西認同為偽斯麥爾地。他們自然也把拉6:14的亞達薛西也視為偽斯麥爾地。其實這裡所指的的國王是亞達薛西一世，有兩個理由：一，很難想象斯麥爾地在顯示敵意以後，在七個月的統治期間裡還會發佈一個善意的諭旨。二，這裡的亞達薛西列在大流士之後。到了以斯拉的年代，居魯士、大流士和亞達薛西都發布過有關聖殿及其崇祀的諭旨。亞達薛西的諭旨中要求聖殿完工的話和第15節中聖殿在大流士治下“修成了”的話表面上有矛盾。但這個表面上的矛盾可以通過合理的推測來解決：亞達薛西對聖殿的裝修（拉7:27），是真正意義上聖殿的竣工。所以以斯拉覺得有理由將亞達薛西列為發佈諭旨，重建聖殿和耶路撒冷的第三個國王（拉7:27；9:9）。
這一節提及亞達薛西一世，證明《以斯拉記》不是在所羅巴伯的時代寫的，而是在以斯拉的時代，可能是在亞達薛西治下所寫的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第233頁；《善惡之爭》第326頁；《先知與君王》第607,698頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–19節）**。《先知與君王》第596頁。

9.en:
**Bullocks, and rams, and lambs.** These were the chief sacrificial animals of the Jews—a lamb being required every morning and evening, 2 more on the Sabbath, 7 at each of the great feasts and at the beginning of each month, and 14 on every day during the Feast of Tabernacles. This would be altogether more than a thousand in the course of a year. Rams and bullocks were added to the lambs on the more solemn occasions. The only other ordinary sacrificial animal was “a kid of the goats.”
Wheat, salt, wine, and oil. These commodities were needed for the “meat offerings” by which every burnt offering was accompanied (Ex. 29:40, 41; see on Lev. 2:13).
According to the appointment. It was a most extraordinary concession to the Jews to allow their priests to fix the amount of support they should receive from the satrap. Darius must have had confidence that the Jews would not abuse his generosity. The integrity of men such as Daniel, Mordecai, Ezra, Nehemiah, and perhaps others, doubtless had made a deep impression on the monarchs under whom they served. It seems probable that some influential Jews were employed in the state department of the Persian Empire. The hand of one of these men probably had part in the preparation of this decree of Darius.
9.zh:
他們與天上的神獻燔祭所需用的公牛犢、公綿羊、綿羊羔，並所用的麥子、鹽、酒、油，都要照耶路撒冷祭司的話，每日供給他們，不得有誤；

**公牛犢、公綿羊、綿羊羔。**是猶太人的主要祭牲：每天早晚要獻羊羔，安息日再加兩頭；每次大節期開始和每個月初要獻七頭；住棚節期間每日獻十四頭。一年獻羊的總數超過一千頭。公綿羊和公牛犢是在更加莊嚴的場合加在羊羔上的。其他普通的祭牲還有“公山羊”。
**麥子、鹽、酒、油。**用於伴隨燔祭的“素祭”（出29:40,41；見利2:13註釋）。
**照耶路撒冷祭司的話。**讓猶太人的祭司來決定從省長那裡得多少物資，這是對於猶太人不尋常的讓步。大流士一定相信猶太人不會濫用他的慷慨。像但以理，末底改，以斯拉和尼希米等正直的人，無疑給他們所服侍的國王留下了深刻的印象。可能有一些有影響力的猶太人在波斯帝國的國家部門工作。他們當中可能有人參與了擬訂大流士的這個諭旨。

1.en:
**Then Darius.** The request of Tatnai, deputy satrap of “Beyond the River,” received the immediate attention of Darius (ch. 5:17).
Made a decree. Preferably, “gave an order,” since a “decree” was not necessary in order to have a search made in the royal archives for the document.
House of the rolls. Literally, “in the house of the books,” that is, the royal library or archives. On the observation that the “treasures” were kept there, see on ch. 5:17.
In Babylon. Tatnai seems to have received the impression from the Jews during his visit in Jerusalem that the original document would probably be found in the royal archives at Babylon. He had suggested, therefore, that Babylon was the place where the search should be made (ch. 5:17). Darius followed this suggestion and had a search made at Babylon, which, however, proved to be fruitless.
1.zh:
於是大利烏王降旨，要尋察典籍庫內，就是在巴比倫藏寶物之處；

**於是大利烏王。**“河西的”總督達乃的申請馬上受到大流士的關注（拉5:17）。
**降旨。**譯為“下令”更好，因為查閱王室檔案無需“降旨”。
**典籍庫。**即“書庫”。就是王室圖書館或檔案庫。還可能保存著財寶，見拉5:17註釋。
**在巴比倫。**達乃似乎在訪問耶路撒冷期間從猶太人那裡得到印象，以為諭旨原件可能保存在巴比倫的王室檔案裡。所以他建議到巴比倫去尋找（拉5:17）。大流士接受了他的建議，結果找不到。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《先知與君王》第579頁。

10.en: **Pray.** The requirement that the good will and generosity of the king be repaid by sacrifices and prayers on his behalf is closely paralleled in the clay barrel inscription of Cyrus already mentioned (see on ch. 1:2). There the king states that he had restored the cult of the Babylonian gods that the Babylonians might daily ask Bel and Nabu to bless him and his son Cambyses with long life. That the Jews were not opposed to carrying out such a request can be concluded from the practice in the time of the Maccabees to offer sacrifices on behalf of the Seleucid kings (1 Macc 7:33).
10.zh:
好叫他們獻馨香的祭給天上的神，又為王和王眾子的壽命祈禱。

要求用獻祭和祈禱來報答國王的善意和慷慨，其語氣很像上述居魯士泥桶的銘文（見拉1:2註釋）。那裡說國王修復了巴比倫的神像，好讓巴比倫人每日求彼勒和拿布賜給他和他兒子岡比西斯長壽。猶太人不會反對這樣的要求，因為在後來馬加比時代他們也曾為塞琉西國王獻祭（《馬加比上》7:33）。

8.en:
**I make a decree.** Darius was not content to send a copy of Cyrus’ decree to Tatnai, to inform him of the right of the Jews to continue working on the Temple. He confirmed the former decree by a new one of his own, one that surpassed even the generous provisions of the former one (see on ch. 1:7).
Expenses. Cyrus had decreed that the reconstruction of the Temple at Jerusalem be subsidized with public funds (v. 4). This part of the decree had probably never been carried out (see ch. 4:4, 5), because the Samaritans seem to have successful in frustrating the good intentions of Cyrus. When Darius learned from the copy of Cyrus’ decree found at Ecbatana that financial support had been promised the Jews, he probably inquired of the royal treasurer as to how much money had been spent on the Temple since the first decree was issued. His annoyance upon receiving the information that either little or nothing had been paid so far is implied by the strong language of his letter to Tatnai—“be ye far from thence” (v. 6), “let the work … alone” (v. 7), “that they be not hindered” (v. 8), “without fail” (v. 9), and especially the threats in v. 11 in case this decree should be ignored.
Cyrus had only vaguely defined the source of financial help as “the king’s house” (v. 4), which could mean that the funds were to come from the royal purse, though all public money was disbursed at the discretion of the king. Darius, however, ordered that the expenses of the men employed on the Temple be paid by the satrap of “Beyond the River” from the royal tribute of the province. Thus, presumably, no additional burden was laid upon the taxpayers.
Many modern commentators have doubted the genuineness of this part of the decree, declaring it unthinkable that a Persian king could be so much interested in the Temple of a distant and insignificant nation. However, secular history presents us with parallel cases. This was Cyrus’ policy not only in regard to the Temple at Jerusalem but also in regard to many other sanctuaries (see on ch. 1:2). It is reported that after conquering Egypt, Cambyses, Cyrus’ son, had the temple of Neith at Saïs cleaned, assured its priesthood of their customary income, and favored it with royal gifts—as the Egyptian kings had done before. Even Antiochus the Great gave the Jews large gifts of wine, oil, incense, wheat, and salt for sacrifices, and money for the completion of the Temple (Antiquities xii. 3. 3), in appreciation of their loyalty early in his reign.
8.zh:
我又降旨，吩咐你們向猶大人的長老為建造神的殿當怎樣行，就是從河西的款項中，急速撥取貢銀作他們的經費，免得耽誤工作。

**我又降旨。**大流士並不滿足於把居魯士諭旨的副本交給達乃，告訴他猶太人有權繼續聖殿的工程。他還發布了一道新的諭旨，不但確認原先的諭旨，而且超越了原先諭旨的慷慨條款（見拉1:7註釋）。
**經費。**居魯士曾下令用公共基金幫助在耶路撒冷聖殿的重建（第4節）。諭旨的這個部分可能從未得到執行（見拉4:4,5），因為撒瑪利亞人阻擾居魯士的善意。大流士從伊克巴塔納的居魯士諭旨副本中瞭解到曾有在經濟上支持猶太人的承諾，可能就詢問國庫官員，從第一次諭旨發佈以來，究竟為聖殿撥了多少款。當他得知迄今為止撥款很少，甚至沒有時，就很生氣。這可以從他給達乃信函的強硬語氣中看出來：“你們當遠離他們”（第6節），“不要攔阻”（第7節），“免得耽誤工作”（第8節），“不得有誤”（第9節）。特別是第11節，宣佈了違背這個諭旨的懲罰。
居魯士只是大致規定財政的支援來自“王庫”（第4節），可能是來自國王個人的資金，儘管所有的公共經費都是由國王支配的。大流士則下令聖殿所僱人員的開支，均由“河西”總督從該省上繳王室的貢稅裡支付。因而不會給納稅人增加額外的負擔。
許多現代註釋家懷疑這道諭旨的真實性，宣稱無法想像一個波斯國王會如此關心一個遙遠小國的聖殿。但世俗歷史也向我們提供了類似的例子。居魯士的政策不僅涉及耶路撒冷的聖殿，也涉及其他許多聖殿（見拉1:2註釋）。據報道，居魯士的兒子岡比西斯在征服埃及以後，潔淨了塞伊斯的內特神廟，保障了其中祭司的日常收入，並且賜給他們若干王室的禮物，就像以前的埃及國王那樣。就連安條克大帝也曾送給猶太人大量的酒，油，香料，麥子和鹽作為祭物，併為聖殿竣工捐錢（《上古史》xii.3.3），以回報猶太人在他統治初期對他的忠誠。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–12節）**。《先知與君王》第598頁；《給傳道人的證言》第203頁。

2.en:
**Found at Achmetha.** When the document referred to in Tatnai’s letter was not found, a further order was apparently given to extend the search to the royal archives of the other Persian capital cities, Ecbatana and Susa. This indicates a sincere effort on the part of the king and his officials to be fair, and to make a thorough investigation before reaching a decision. This places the Persians in a most favorable light. They could easily have discontinued the search upon finding, at Babylon, no decree of Cyrus regarding the Jews. In extending the search to other places where it was apparently known that official documents of Cyrus’ first year were deposited, these officials did everything possible to arrive at a fair and unbiased conclusion.
Achmetha was the old Median capital. In Old Persian it was called Hagmatâna, and in Greek, Ecbatana. Today the city is called Hamadân. Lying in the western Iranian mountains, 6,000 ft. (1,829 m.) above sea level, the Persian kings made it one of their summer capitals. Babylon, situated in the river valley, became uncomfortably hot in summer. The present population of Hamadân is more than 100,000.
The fact that the document was found in Ecbatana and not in Babylon indicates that Cyrus resided there when the decree was issued. The relation of this fact to the date of issuance of the decree has already been noted in comments on ch. 1:1.
A roll. All documents of the Persian Empire period which have been recovered from the region of Mesopotamia and Persia are cuneiform tablets. Owing to the climatic conditions prevailing in these lands, Persian records written on perishable material such as papyrus or leather have not survived. However, Persian documents on papyrus and leather from that period have been preserved in Egypt, proving the accuracy of the statement here made that the official decree of Cyrus was written on a scroll, not on a clay tablet. Since the official, universal language of the Persian Empire was Aramaic, as the documents found in Egypt testify, it can be taken for granted that Cyrus’ decree was written in Aramaic.
2.zh:
在瑪代省亞馬他城的宮內尋得一卷，其中記著說：

**亞馬他城的宮內尋得。**達乃的信件裡所提的文件既未找到，國王顯然又下令把調查的範圍擴大到其他的波斯都城伊克巴塔納和蘇沙（書珊）。這說明國王和他的官員處事公正，在做出最後決定以前先進行全面的調查。波斯人的這種做法是值得稱道的。他們在巴比倫沒有找到居魯士有關猶太人的諭旨，本來是可以放棄調查的。但這些官員把調查擴大到其他已知存放居魯士元年官方文件的地方，千方百計想要得出公正的結論。
亞馬他是古代瑪代人的首都。古波斯語為Hagmatâna；希臘語為伊克巴塔納。今稱Hamadân（哈馬丹），在伊朗西部山區，海拔1,829米，是波斯國王的夏都之一。巴比倫位於河谷，夏天十分炎熱，很不舒服。現在Hamadân的人口有十萬多。
文件不在巴比倫，而在伊克巴塔納發現，說明居魯士是在伊克巴塔納發佈該諭旨的。關於該諭旨發佈的時間和地點的關係，見拉1:1註釋。
**一卷。**在美索不達米亞和波斯地區所發現的所有波斯帝國時期的文獻都是楔形文字的字板。由於這些地區的氣候條件，記錄在易腐材料，如紙莎草紙或皮捲上的波斯文獻均已不存在。但是，當時記在紙莎草紙或皮捲上的波斯文獻卻在埃及保存了下來，證實這裡所說居魯士的諭旨是寫在皮捲上，而不是在泥板上的話。埃及發現的文獻證實，波斯帝國官方通用的語言是亞蘭語，故可以確定居魯士的諭旨是用亞蘭語書寫的。

5.en: **The golden and silver vessels.** See on ch. 1:7–11.
5.zh:
並且神殿的金銀器皿，就是尼布甲尼撒從耶路撒冷的殿中掠到巴比倫的，要歸還帶到耶路撒冷的殿中，各按原處放在神的殿裡。

見拉1:7-11註釋。

11.en:
**Hanged.** Not hanging as we know it, but impaling, a cruel form of execution practiced extensively by the Assyrians. Many of their reliefs depict impaled men, mostly captured enemies. Two ways of impaling were known. In each, a stake with a sharp point was set up in the ground. The victim, nude, was then impaled by piercing him through his body, either from his buttocks upward or through his chest.
Threats such as those Darius attached to this decree are common in ancient documents. In the light of the practice of absolute rulers in ancient times the threats in this decree do not seem extraordinary. People reading royal decrees in the ancient Orient were used to them, and often witnessed their execution. For example, the famous code of Hammurabi contains some 250 lines of imprecations against any who should alter its provisions. Darius felt that his decree was in need of strong language. The Samaritans had shown themselves clever in the art of defying royal commands. The decree was intended to frighten them, and thereby restrain them from doing further harm.
11.zh:
我再降旨，無論誰更改這命令，必從他房屋中拆出一根梁來，把他舉起，懸在其上，又使他的房屋成為糞堆。

不是絞刑，而是刺刑，是亞述人流行的殘忍的處決方式。他們的浮雕中有許多受刺刑的人，主要是戰俘的畫面。已知的刺刑有兩種，均在地上豎立起一根削尖的木樁，把裸體的受害者人從臀部向上或橫穿胸部刺入。
大流士在諭旨附加這種威懾，是古代的文獻所常見的。作為古代專制的統治者，在諭旨上附加這樣的威懾非不罕見。看古代東方諭旨的人見慣了這種措辭，並經常目睹其實施。例如著名的漢漠拉比法典，就為想要改變其條款的人列出大約250條咒詛。大流士認為需要加強他諭旨的語氣。撒瑪利亞人善於抵制國王的命令。諭旨是為了威懾他們，使他們不敢破壞。

4.en:
**A row of new timber.** See on ch. 5:8.
The expenses. See on chs. 1:4 and 6:3.
4.zh:
用三層大石頭，一層新木頭，經費要出於王庫；

**一層新木頭。**見拉5:8註釋。
**經費。**見拉1:4至6:3註釋。

7.zh:
不要攔阻神殿的工作，任憑猶大人的省長和猶大人的長老在原處建造神的這殿。

**懷愛倫註釋（7–12節）**。《先知與君王》第579頁。

13.zh:
於是，河西總督達乃和示他波斯乃，並他們的同黨，因大利烏王所發的命令，就急速遵行。

**達乃。**關於這裡所提到的人，見拉5:3,6註釋。
**就急速遵行。**達乃等人以前的舉動和他們寫給大流士的信函，表明他們對猶太人沒有敵意。他們毫不猶豫地執行國王的命令。國王已明確地向他們宣佈自己的旨意。於是他們著手積極執行。他們的善意為聖殿的迅速竣工做出了一定的貢獻。達乃等人一定再次訪問耶路撒冷，瞭解猶太人在經濟上的需求，以及聖殿崇祀所需祭牲的數量（見第9節註釋）。
13.en:
**Tatnai.** Concerning the men here mentioned, see on ch. 5:3, 6.
So they did speedily. Having no enmity toward the Jews, as is evident from their former actions and their letter to Darius, Tatnai and his fellow officers revealed no reluctance in carrying out the royal command. The king’s will had been made known to them in unmistakable words, and they proceeded to carry it out with zeal. In part, the rapid completion of the Temple must be attributed to their good will. This must have required Tatnai and his retinue to visit Jerusalem again and make a survey of the financial needs of the Jews and the number of sacrificial animals considered necessary for the Temple service (see on v. 9).

15.zh:
大利烏王第六年，亞達月初三日，這殿修成了。

聖殿竣工的確切時間，可能就是第16-18節所描述舉行獻殿禮的日子。在大流士一世第六年亞達月（猶大曆六月）初三日，大約是公元前515年3月12日，逾越節前六週。
重建聖殿從第二次立根基之石開始（基斯流月24日，大流士二年）到完工，共花費了約四年零三個月，比所羅門建殿的時間少了兩年零三個月左右。這種差異可能是因為所羅門要先建一個基礎，然後在上面完成聖殿整體的不同建築。這是一個很大的工程。雖然眼前耶路撒冷聖殿的地基可以追溯到希律時代，或晚些時候，但就目前的規模而言，仍能看出早期建築者所付出的巨大努力，建好基礎，然後在上面建造聖殿及其許多輔助建築。當被擄者回歸的時候，可能發現大部分基礎結構依然良好，無須費時耗財予以修復。而且聖殿似乎也不如所羅門時代那樣精緻龐大，裝飾豪華（見拉3:12）。還有一些工程是第一次諭旨以後開展的。由於上述部分或者全部原因，第二聖殿建造的時間相對縮短了。
我們沒有任何有關新殿的規模，輔助性建築的數量及其佈局和外觀的資料。有些部分可能是以所羅門的聖殿或以西結異像中的殿（結40-42章）為藍本的。這個聖殿像所羅門的聖殿一樣有輔助性的建築。因為拉8:29；尼12:44；13:4,5等處提到一些與聖殿相關的房間。有些安放聖殿的財寶，有些作為祭司的辦公室。據《馬加比上》4:38，聖殿周圍有幾個庭院。
15.en:
**Finished.** The exact day of the completion of the Temple is given, probably also the day of dedication described in vs. 16–18. Adar 3 in the 6th regnal year of Darius I was about March 12, 515 .., six weeks before the Passover.
The rebuilding of the Temple from the time the foundation stone had been laid a second time (Kislev 24, 2d year of Darius) to its completion, had therefore occupied about 4 years and 3 months, some 2 years and 3 months shorter than it had taken Solomon to build his Temple. The reason for this difference probably lies in the fact that Solomon had first to prepare a flat surface on which to erect the various buildings belonging to the Temple complex, a task of no small size. Although the present substructures of the Temple area at Jerusalem date from Herodian times or later, as far as they are visible, they reveal the tremendous efforts that must have been made by the early builders to construct a foundation platform on which the Temple and its many auxiliary buildings could be erected. When the exiles returned they probably found that great parts of this substructure were still good enough to use without expensive, time-consuming repair work. Furthermore, the buildings seem to have been less elaborate and numerous than in Solomon’s time, and probably much less lavishly decorated (see ch. 3:12). Also, a certain amount of building had been carried on since the time that the first decree was issued. Some or all of these reasons may have been responsible for the comparatively short period required to build the second Temple.
Concerning the size of the new Temple, the number of subsidiary buildings, their arrangement and outer form, we are completely without information. The Temple of Solomon, or perhaps the ideal temple of Ezekiel (Eze. 40–42), may have served as a pattern for some parts. That this Temple, like Solomon’s, possessed auxiliary buildings, is evident from such texts as Ezra 8:29; Neh. 12:44; 13:4, 5, where certain rooms are mentioned in connection with the Temple. In some of these chambers Temple treasures were kept; others served as offices for certain priests. According to 1 Macc. 4:38 the Temple was surrounded by several courts.

16.zh:
以色列的祭司和利未人，並其餘被擄歸回的人都歡歡喜喜地行奉獻神殿的禮。

這裡簡單描述獻殿禮，只含有以下信息：一，這是一個歡樂的日子；二，奉獻大量祭物；三，聖殿的僕役，祭司和利未人從那天起履行摩西的律法所規定的職責。在奉獻日的活動中，音樂無疑起了重要作用，因為以前的類似場合均伴有大量歌詠（見代上16:4-36；代下29:25-29）。
16.en: **Kept the dedication.** The report of this feast of dedication is brief, containing only the information that (1) it was a feast of joy, (2) a great number of sacrifices were offered, and (3) the Temple servants, priests, and Levites carried out the services prescribed by the law of Moses from that day forth. Music no doubt played a major role in the activities of the day of dedication, inasmuch as there had been much singing connected with similar occasions in earlier times (see 1 Chron. 16:4–36; 2 Chron. 29:25–29).

17.zh:
行奉獻神殿的禮就獻公牛一百隻，公綿羊二百隻，綿羊羔四百隻，又照以色列支派的數目獻公山羊十二隻，為以色列眾人作贖罪祭；

**公牛一百隻。**與所羅門（王上8:63），希西家（代下30:24）和約西亞（代下35:7）治下的類似慶典相比，這次獻殿禮的祭物數量甚少。是以百來計算，而不是以前的千。
**為以色列眾人。**作者謹慎地將回歸者稱為“以色列”，而不只是“猶大”（見拉2:70；3:1；4:3；5:1）。所獻的公山羊是十二頭（拉6:17），代表以色列王國未分裂時的十二支派。我們可以設想各支派都有人隨所羅巴伯迴歸，所以把這些重新組合的人稱為“以色列”（見尼11:20；耶50:4；結37:15-19；亞8:13；瑪1:1）。但迴歸者中猶大支派和便亞憫支派佔多數，故更多被稱為“猶大”（拉4:1,6；5:1；亞8:15）。為了體現更加莊嚴和崇高的理念，把會眾視為全體上帝百姓的餘民，所羅巴伯下令嚴肅的贖罪祭奉獻十二頭公山羊，各代表一個支派。以斯拉六十年以後帶著第二批迴歸者到達耶路撒冷以後，也效仿了這種做法（拉8:35）。
17.en:
**An hundred bullocks.** The number of sacrifices offered during this dedication service is small in comparison with similar services celebrated during the reigns of Solomon (1 Kings 8:63), Hezekiah (2 Chron. 30:24), and Josiah (2 Chron. 35:7). Hundreds now take the place of the thousands previously offered.
All Israel. In v. 16 the congregation is referred to as “the children of Israel.” The writer is careful to present the returned exiles as “Israel,” not merely as “Judah” (see chs. 2:70; 3:1; 4:3; 5:1). The number of he-goats offered was 12 (ch. 6:17), the number of tribes in the undivided kingdom. We may assume that representatives of every tribe had returned with Zerubbabel, and that consequently it was possible to regard the re-established people as “Israel” (see Neh. 11:20; Jer. 50:4; Eze. 37:15–19; Zech. 8:13; Mal. 1:1). However, the great majority of the repatriated exiles were of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and were accordingly more commonly spoken of as “Judah” (Ezra 4:1, 6; 5:1; Zech. 8:15). Desirous of emphasizing the nobler and grander view, of seeing in the congregation the remnants of the whole people of God, Zerubbabel ordered this solemn sin offering of 12 he-goats, one for each of the tribes. Ezra followed the same procedure when he arrived in Jerusalem with the second group of exiles some 60 years later (Ezra 8:35).

18.zh:
且派祭司和利未人按著班次在耶路撒冷事奉神，是照摩西律法書上所寫的。

新殿完工以後，自然就要按照原先大衛的方式安排聖殿工作人員（見代上23:6-23；24:1-9）。這種安排的依據《民數記》的律法有關祭司和利未人兩等人員的規定（民3:6-10；8:6-26）.但是“班次”則是大衛的時代制訂的。
18.en: **Priests in their divisions.** The completion of the new Temple was naturally followed by an arrangement of the ministers of the Temple, corresponding to that originally made by David (see 1 Chron. 23:6–23; 24:1–9). This arrangement was based upon the ordinances of the law concerning the respective offices of the two orders— priests and Levites—as given in the book of Numbers (chs. 3:6–10; 8:6–26), but the “courses” themselves were not established till David’s time.

19.zh:
正月十四日，被擄歸回的人守逾越節。

**正月十四日。**這是摩西的律法所規定的日子（見出12:6）。約為公元前515年4 月21日。
**守逾越節。**值得注意的是從本節開始,作者又恢復使用希伯來語，直到拉7:11。以斯拉的書一部分用希伯來語，一部分用了亞蘭語，最簡單的解釋就是對兩種語言猶太人都熟悉。亞蘭語是波斯帝國的通用語。官方的法令都用它來寫。
在猶太人的歷史上，有幾次非常嚴肅的逾越節慶典，受到聖經作者的特別關注。如希西家潔淨聖殿以後逾越節的慶祝（代下30章），約西亞完成改革以後的慶祝（代下35章）。這兩次逾越節都發生在一段期間的背道以後，伴隨著聖殿崇拜的復興。以斯拉也把逾越節的慶祝安排在奉獻新殿以後。這並不意味著被擄者在公元前515年以前沒有慶祝逾越節。拉3:5說他們一回到故鄉，就遵守“耶和華的一切聖節”。但新殿竣工後的第一個逾越節標誌著完全恢復正常的宗教儀式。這些儀式在第一聖殿被毀以後多少被中斷了。
19.en:
**Kept the passover.** It should be noted that wish this verse the author returns to the use of Hebrew, and continues in Hebrew till ch. 7:11. That Ezra wrote parts of his book in Hebrew and parts in Aramaic may probably be most simply explained by the fact that both languages were well known to the Jews. Aramaic was the language common to the Persian Empire. Official decrees were written in it.
A number of particularly solemn Passovers were celebrated in Jewish history, and these were accorded special attention by the writers of the Bible. Such are the Passover celebrated by Hezekiah after his cleansing of the Temple (2 Chron. 30), and that celebrated by Josiah after the completion of his reform (2 Chron. 35). Both of these Passovers accompanied a revival of Temple worship after a period of apostasy. Ezra places in the same category the Passover following the dedication of the new Temple. This does not mean that the exiles had not celebrated the Passover prior to the year 515 .., since Ezra 3:5 contains the information that they observed “all the set feasts of the Lord” as soon as they arrived in their homeland. However, this first Passover after the completion of the building of the new Temple marked the full re-establishment of the regular ordinances of religion, more or less interrupted from the time of the destruction of the first Temple.
Fourteenth day. The day fixed by the law of Moses (see Ex. 12:6). This was about April 21, 515 ..

20.zh:
原來，祭司和利未人一同自潔，無一人不潔淨。利未人為被擄歸回的眾人和他們的弟兄眾祭司，並為自己宰逾越節的羊羔。

有些註釋家贊同以下的譯文：“祭司潔淨了自己，利未人都是潔淨的，如同一人”。他們認為在第20節後半句裡，利未人是為祭司和平民“宰逾越節的羊羔”的。代下29:34說到在希西家的時代，利未人比祭司更加潔淨。但大多數譯者認為這裡沒有區分祭司和利未人。他們都是聖殿的服務人員，共同為這莊嚴的時刻作準備。祭司和利未人一起宰殺逾越節的羔羊。
20.en: **Purified together.** The translation of v. 20 as given in the KJV and RSV is probably correct, though the following has been defended by a number of commentators: “For the priests had purified themselves, while the Levites were all pure, as one man.” Those who follow the latter translation believe that the Levites are the ones referred to in the second half of v. 20 as killing the Passover for both priests and laymen, being more completely sanctified than the priests. Such a situation is described in 2 Chron. 29:34, where the Levites in the time of Hezekiah are described as being more upright in heart than the priests. However, most translators follow the KJV reading. This reading makes no difference between the priests and Levites, holding that both classes of Temple attendants were equally prepared for this solemn occasion, and presents priests and Levites as working together in the slaying of the Passover lambs.

21.zh:
從擄到之地歸回的以色列人和一切除掉所染外邦人汙穢、歸附他們、要尋求耶和華─以色列神的人都吃這羊羔，

在講述了迴歸的被擄者以後，以斯拉在這裡提到慶祝逾越節另一批以色列人。他們一定是“民中最窮的”， 在公元前586年被尼布甲尼撒留下來“修理葡萄園，耕種田地”的人（王下25:12）。在漫長的被擄期間，祭司和宗教領袖都在巴比倫。這些無知貧窮的人似乎接受了許多異教的習俗。被擄者在患難的學校受到但以理和以西結等人有益的影響，體驗了新的宗教經驗。他們自然要求沒有去巴比論的人改變自己的生活，以便適應新的狀態。其中可能還有完全接受猶太人宗教的外邦人。他們被平等地接納到猶太人的會眾之中。在出埃及時，就已為所有希望加入上帝子民的外邦人，制定了這樣的條款。
21.en: **Separated themselves.** Having mentioned the returned exiles, Ezra here refers to a second group of Israelites as taking part in the celebration of the Passover. These must have been some of “the poor of the land,” left behind by Nebuchadnezzar in 586 .. “to be vinedressers and husbandmen” (2 Kings 25:12). During the long years of exile, when the priests and religious leaders were in Babylon, these ignorant, poor people seem to have accepted many pagan practices. The exiles had gained a new religious experience in the school of tribulation under the wholesome influence of men like Daniel and Ezekiel. Accordingly they required those who had not been to Babylon to reform their lives in order to belong to the new state. Some of those here referred to may have been foreigners who wholeheartedly accepted the religion of the Jews, and were received into the congregation of the Jews as equals. As at the time of the Exodus, provision was made for all of those who desired to join God’s people, to do so.

22.zh:
歡歡喜喜地守除酵節七日；因為耶和華使他們歡喜，又使亞述王的心轉向他們，堅固他們的手，作以色列神殿的工程。

**除酵節。**按照律法，這個節日要守七天（出12:15；13:7；利23:6）。關於這個節日的屬靈意義，見林前5:8。
**亞述王。**一般認為這裡是指大流士。他被稱為“亞述王”有點奇怪。波斯王們從來沒有稱自己是“亞述王”。儘管從居魯士到薛西斯，他們的名號上還加上“巴比倫王”。由於巴比倫多世紀以來曾歸屬亞述，最後推翻了波斯帝國，佔領了其所有的領土。所以有可能用亞述來表示巴比倫（見王下23:29註釋）。
根據另一種解釋，這裡的亞述僅代表西亞的大國，按照所說的時代，可以是指巴比倫，波斯，或者其他國家。最近所發現兩約之間的文獻支持這個觀點。該文獻稱塞琉西的國王為亞述人。
22.en:
**Feast of unleavened bread.** This was observed for one week, as required by the law (Ex. 12:15; 13:7; Lev. 23:6). On the spiritual meaning of the feast see 1 Cor. 5:8.
King of Assyria. It is generally understood that Darius is meant here, and it is surprising to find him called “king of Assyria.” It is true that the Persian kings never called themselves “King of Assyria,” although from Cyrus until Xerxes they bore the title “King of Babylon” in addition to their other titles. Since Babylon had been part of Assyria for centuries, but had finally replaced that empire, occupying all its former possessions, it is possible that the name Assyria is here used as a synonym for Babylonia (see on 2 Kings 23:29).
According to another interpretation, Assyria here is simply a designation for the great power of Western Asia, whether at the time the statement was made this power might be Babylonia, Persia, or some other power. Support for this view is found in recently discovered documents of the intertestament period, in which the Seleucid kings are called Assyrians.

15.en:
**The silver and gold.** Financial affairs assume a most important role in this decree. Gifts which Ezra was commissioned to take to Jerusalem came from three sources—the king and his counselors, a collection taken among non-Jewish friends in the satrapy of Babylonia, and freewill offerings made by Jews resident outside of Palestine (v. 16). In ancient times the transmission of great sums of money was made by well-protected caravans. The highways of travel were never safe from robbers, and the larger the remittance the greater the danger of its being intercepted. Josephus relates (Antiquities xviii. 9. 1) that the gifts annually remitted to Jerusalem from Babylon in Roman times were escorted by a great number of armed men.
Whose habitation. This phrase is similar, but not identical, to that used by Cyrus in ch. 1:2, 3. It does not necessarily mean that Artaxerxes considered the God of the Jews a local deity, but simply that the location of His Temple was at Jerusalem. If a Jew such as Ezra was the the actual author of this decree, which was then approved by Artaxerxes (see v. 12), he would naturally use phraseology such as this.
15.zh:
又帶金銀，就是王和謀士甘心獻給住耶路撒冷、以色列神的，

**金銀。**財政問題在這道諭旨裡佔重要位置。以斯拉負責帶到耶路撒冷的禮物有三個來源：國王和他的謀士的禮物；巴比倫地區非猶太人朋友的捐助；巴勒斯坦地區以外猶太人的樂意奉獻（第16節）。在古代，運送大筆金銀需要有武裝保護的車隊。一路上會有強盜。金額越大，受到伏擊的危險就越大。約瑟弗斯說（《上古史》xviii.9.1），在羅馬時代，每年從巴比倫送往耶路撒冷的禮物都需要有大批武裝人員的護送。
**耶路撒冷、以色列上帝。**這個說法與拉1:2,3中居魯士的話相似，但不完全一樣。不一定指亞達薛西把猶太人的上帝視為地區的神，而只是說明祂聖殿的位置是在耶路撒冷。如果像以斯拉這樣的猶太人是亞達薛西所指定的諭旨執筆者（第12節），他自然會用這樣的措辭。

12.en:
**King of kings.** The decree itself is quoted in vs. 12–26, written in Aramaic exactly as it issued from the Persian chancellery. It is closely related in form and content to the documents found in chs. 4 to 6, and is now, following the discovery of similar documents in Elephantine, recognized as genuine by even the most critical scholar. “Kings of kings” was a recognized title of the Persian monarchs, and is found in every Persian inscription of any considerable length. The title was first used by Assyrian kings, who thereby expressed the fact that they ruled over many vassal kings whom they retained on their respective thrones in conquered lands. The title was later taken over by the kings of Babylon (see Dan. 2:37), and then by the Persian kings when they became masters of the world.
Ezra the priest. It is interesting to note that the decree does not make use of the ordinary Aramaic word kumra’, “priest,” but the loan word kahen, taken from the Heb. kohen. In Aramaic documents from Elephantine, writers also make a clear distinction between pagan priests, for whom they used the ordinary Aramaic word kumra’, and the true priests of God, whom they designated by the word, kahana’. The use of this word in the document of Ezra 7 therefore indicates that the decree, although approved and issued by the king and in his name, was composed by a Jew in the imperial chancellery. Other evidence found in this decree points in the same direction.
A scribe of the law of the God of heaven. Aramaic, saphar datha’ di–’elah shemayya’. A correct explanation of this title was made in the 1930’s by H. H. Schaeder. On the basis of analogous titles he shows that it designates a high officer in the Persian chancellery in charge of affairs pertaining to “the law of the God of heaven.” Accordingly, Ezra was a reporter of Jewish religious affairs in the Persian government. Similarly we find in the later Parthian and Sassanide government the head of the Jewish population (resh galutha’, “head of the exiles”) occasionally ranking with the highest government officials. Neh. 11:24 also testifies to the existence of such an office in the time of Artaxerxes I. We are unable to say how Ezra received this appointment, but it is evident that appointment to this office would make him the most influential Jew in Babylon. That he used his influence in the interest of his people is proved by the contents of the decree.
Perfect. The Aramaic has only the word gemir, meaning “completed,” and is considered by most scholars to be either an abbreviated formula indicating the end of a document or a word meaning “issued.” In the first case the word “peace” must be supplied, as the KJV has done, but the second interpretation considers the text complete as it stands.
And at such a time. See on ch. 4:17.
12.zh:
諸王之王亞達薛西，達於祭司以斯拉通達天上神律法大德的文士，云云。

**諸王之王。**第12-26節的諭旨，採用了波斯王室文告的原文亞蘭語。其形式和內容十分接近非常拉4至6章中的文件。現在根據厄勒番丁島所發現的類似文件，即使是最挑剔的學者，也會確認它的真實性。“諸王之王”是波斯君主眾所周知的稱號，在任何具有一定篇幅的波斯銘文中均有這個稱號。該稱號最早為亞述王所使用，以表明他們統治著許多臣屬的國王。那些國王是他們在所征服的國家裡保留下來的。這個稱號後來相繼有歸屬統治天下的巴比倫國王（見但2:37）和波斯國王。
**祭司以斯拉。**值得注意的是這個諭旨沒有使用亞蘭語通用的kumra'（祭司），而是使用源於希伯來語kohen的kahen。在厄勒番丁島的亞蘭語文獻中，作者明顯區別了異教祭司（用通常的亞蘭語kumra'）和上帝的真祭司（用kahana'）。在拉7章的文獻裡使用該詞，說明雖然這個諭旨是國王以他的名義頒佈的，但撰寫者會是帝國內閣中的一位猶太人。本諭旨中的其他證據也證明這一點。
**通達天上上帝律法大德的文士。**亞蘭語是saphar datha' di-'elah shemayya'。謝德（H.H.Schaeder）在20世紀30年代正確解讀了這個稱呼。他通過類似稱呼的比較，認為這是指波斯內閣中負責有關“天上上帝律法” 事務的高級官員。所以以斯拉是波斯政府中猶太人宗教事務的報告人。同樣，我們在後來的帕提亞王朝和薩桑王朝（公元226-651，波斯王朝）政府裡，也發現有猶太人的領袖（resh galutha'，“流亡者之首”）列在政府的最高官員中間。尼11:24也證明在亞達薛西一世時代存在這樣的職務。我們不知道以斯拉是如何得到了這個任命的。但這個職務顯然他成為一個在巴比倫地區最有影響的猶太人。諭旨的內容證明了他利用自己的影響力為同胞謀利益。
**云云。**亞蘭語是gemir，意為“已完成”。大多數學者認為這是公文結尾的縮略形式，或意為“已發”。如果是前一種含義，須加“平安”（中文聖經為“德”），後一種含義就不需要加了。
原文還有“那時“。見拉4:17註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–13節）**。《先知與君王》第607頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（12–26節）**。《善惡之爭》第326頁；《懷愛倫傳略》第58頁；《證言》卷一第52頁。

19.en: **The vessels also.** It does not appear that these were sacred vessels originally belonging to the first Temple, like those Cyrus had entrusted to Zerubbabel. Rather, it would seem, they were part of the voluntary offering (v. 15), in which they are distinctly included (see ch. 8:26–28). Perhaps the vessels sent with Zerubbabel had proved too few for the great festivals. There are parallels in ancient history, of kings sending expensive vessels as gifts to other kings, or to the temples of allied nations. Artaxerxes’ gift was thus by no means unusual.
19.zh:
所交給你神殿中使用的器皿，你要交在耶路撒冷神面前。

這些器皿似乎不是指第一聖殿的聖器，如居魯士交給所羅巴伯的那些。而有可能是樂意奉獻的一部分（第15節）。見拉8:26-28。也許交給所羅巴伯的器皿，不夠大節期使用。在古代歷史上，常有一個國王向其他國王，或盟國的廟宇贈送珍貴的器皿作為禮物。亞達薛西的禮物不是異乎尋常的。

26.en: **Let judgment be executed.** Finally, Ezra was authorized to enforce the law, with the power to fine, imprison, banish, or execute offenders, as he should deem right. These powers were always entrusted by the Persians to the civil administrators of provinces, who ruled as autocrats within their respective territories, responsible to the king alone. The grant of such far-reaching responsibilities to Ezra shows that Artaxerxes did not consider him merely a religious leader. He was invested with secular authority over every branch of the administration of the Judean province, except, perhaps, that of finance.
26.zh:
凡不遵行你神律法和王命令的人就當速速定他的罪，或治死，或充軍，或抄家，或囚禁。

**定他的罪。**最後以斯拉還獲得了執法權，在必要時可以懲罰，拘禁，驅逐，或處決罪犯。波斯人總是把這些權力交託給各省的行政長官，讓他們的各自的轄地裡執掌絕對的大權，而且只對國王一個人負責。託付給以斯拉這麼大的權利，說明亞達薛西不單把他看作一位宗教領袖。他被授予世俗的權力，管理猶大省各部門的行政工作，但財政權可能除外。

14.en:
**Seven counselors.** In Esther 1:14 the seven counselors appear as seven princes, who “saw the king’s face” and “sat the first in the kingdom.” No inscriptions have thus far been found to explain further the functions of this group. The conjecture has been made that it refers to the heads of the seven great Persian families, which, according to Herodotus (iii. 84), had privileges that went beyond those enjoyed by other families, including the right of unrestricted access to the royal presence.
The law of thy God. Ezra’s commission included the duty of carrying out an investigation into the religious conditions in the province of Judea. For this, the law of God would, of course, be made the standard. The words concerning the law have frequently been understood by critical scholars as implying that Ezra was the author, or at least an editor, of the law referred to. That this view is incorrect can be seen from v. 25, which indicates that this law was already well known to the Palestinian Jews before Ezra’s arrival. It is therefore obvious that “the law of thy God” was a book, or books, already in the possession of Ezra, and of the Jews in Palestine as well. The nature of this law, already known to the Jews of Babylon and Palestine, is revealed in Neh. 8.
14.zh:
王與七個謀士既然差你去，照你手中神的律法書察問猶大和耶路撒冷的景況；

**七個謀士。**據斯1:13，七個謀士就是七位大臣。他們“常見王面”，是“國中坐高位的”。迄今尚無其他文獻進一步解釋這些人的作用。有人推測他們是波斯七大家族的首領。希羅多德說（iii.84），他們的權利超過其他的家族，包括有權不受限制地晉見國王。
**上帝的律法書。**以斯拉的任務包括對猶大省的宗教狀況進行調查。上帝的律法當然成為調查的標準。批評家們常以這裡有關律法的話認定以斯拉是律法的作者，或至少是編者。25節否定了這種看法。該處說明巴勒斯坦的猶太人在以斯拉來到以前早已十分了解律法。所以“上帝的律法書”是指以斯拉手中，或巴勒斯坦的猶太人手中的書。尼8章說明巴比倫和巴勒斯坦的猶太人已經瞭解這部律法的性質。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–23節）**。《先知與君王》第610頁。

24.en:
**We certify.** The older commentators have seen in the pronoun “we” either a plural of majesty, still in common use by royalty and perhaps comparable to the editorial “we,” or an indication that Artaxerxes here includes his sons. Both views, however, are incorrect. A better understanding of Aramaic shows that the subject of the active participle “certify,” or “notify,” is indefinite, and that the phrase should be translated in the passive sense “you are notified.”
It shall not be lawful. On the three taxes mentioned here see on ch. 4:13. Documentary evidence reveals that the Egyptian priesthood was exempt from taxes during most of its history (see on Gen. 47:22). Although there is no documentary evidence confirming the same custom in Persia, the fact that this privilege was granted to the Jewish Temple personnel implies that the Persian priesthood also was tax exempt. Ezra would hardly have secured such a grant for the priests of his people if the Persian priesthood had not enjoyed similar privileges.
That the policy of exempting priests from taxation is not without parallel even in the time of the Persians can be seen from a Greek inscription in which Darius I censures a certain Gadatas for ignoring the royal policy by exacting “tribute from the sacred cultivators of Apollo.” Antiochus the Great also granted similar privileges to the Jewish priesthood (Josephus Antiquities xii. 3. 3).
24.zh:
我又曉諭你們，至於祭司、利未人、歌唱的、守門的，和尼提寧，並在神殿當差的人，不可叫他們進貢，交課，納稅。

**我又曉諭你們。**有文本為“我們曉諭你們”。過去的註釋家認為“我們”是現在依然使用的表示皇家的複數，與報刊編輯用的“我們”相似，或亞達薛西在這裡包括他的兒子們。但這兩種看法都不對。在亞蘭語中，主動語態的分詞“曉諭”的主語是泛指的。所以該句可譯為“曉諭你們”。
**不可叫他們進貢，交課，納稅。**這裡提到的三種稅見拉4:13註釋。文獻表明，埃及的祭司在歷史上大都是免稅的（見創47:22註釋）。雖然沒有文獻證明波斯有同樣的做法，但猶太的聖殿人員得到了這個權利，說明波斯的祭司也是免稅的。如果波斯的祭司沒有這種特權，以斯拉就很難為猶太祭司爭取這樣的權利。
從一份希臘的銘文中可以看出，祭司免稅的政策在波斯的時代不是沒有先例的。該銘文說大流士一世責備一個叫加達塔（Gadatas）的人無視王室的政策，“向阿波羅的神聖祭司收稅”。安條克大帝也曾給予猶太祭司相似的特權（約瑟弗斯《上古史》xii.3.3）。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–26節）**。《先知與君王》第611頁。

18.en: **Whatsoever shall seem good.** The remainder of the money was to be spent in any way that Ezra, acting under divine guidance, might direct. Ezra was thus free to use as much of the money as he deemed wise for purposes he might consider necessary, without asking specific permission each time. The decree thus gave him the right to use money for such things as repair work on the Temple or for rebuilding the wall. At the time the decree was written Ezra may have considered this freedom of action desirable. Later, when the Samaritans showed their enmity, he may have regretted not having specific objectives mentioned in the decree that were to be financed with the royal appropriation.
18.zh:
剩下的金銀，你和你的弟兄看著怎樣好，就怎樣用，總要遵著你們神的旨意。

剩餘的資金讓以斯拉遵照上帝的指示使用。以斯拉可以按照自己認為合理的判斷隨意使用資金，不必每次都謀求批准。諭旨授權他把可以資金用於修復聖殿或重建城牆等工程。在寫諭旨的時候，以斯拉可能認為需要有這種自由的行動權。後來當撒瑪利亞人與他們作對時，他可能後悔沒有在諭旨中寫明王室撥款的具體項目。

23.en:
**Wrath against the realm.** In the seventh year of Artaxerxes I there was “wrath against the realm” of Persia of a most serious nature. Egypt had revolted from the Persians c. 463 .., and in the following year, with the assistance of the Athenians, had driven the last Persian out of the country. Toward the close of 459 a vain attempt was made to force Athens to recall her troops. In 458 Artaxerxes resolved to attempt the recovery of the revolted country. Soon thereafter he issued this decree authorizing Ezra’s expedition to Jerusalem. History records that from the year 457 .. on things went well for the Persians in Egypt. Memphis was recovered in that year, and in 456 the Athenian troops were finally defeated and the province of Egypt recovered.
And his sons. When Artaxerxes came to the throne he was still quite young, and it is not known how many sons he had in his seventh year. Ultimately, the number reached 18 (Ctesias Excursus Persika 44).
23.zh:
凡天上之神所吩咐的，當為天上神的殿詳細辦理。為何使忿怒臨到王和王眾子的國呢？

**忿怒臨到。**亞達薛西一世七年，十分嚴重的“憤怒臨到”波斯。約公元前463年，埃及背叛波斯。第二年在雅典人的幫助下把波斯人趕出埃及。公元前459年底，亞達薛西想迫使雅典人撤回部隊，但沒有成功。公元前458年，亞達薛西決心收復失地。此後不久，他發佈諭旨，授權以斯拉前往耶路撒冷。史載從公元前457年開始，波斯人在埃及進展順利。當年收復了孟斐斯（聖經中為“摩弗”），並於公元前456年最終打敗雅典軍隊，恢復了埃及省。
**王眾子的。**亞達薛西登基時還很年輕。不知道他在位七年時有幾個兒子。他後來共有18個兒子（Ctesias： Excursus Persika 44）。

27.en:
**Blessed.** Having quoted the important document in Aramaic, the language in which it was originally issued, Ezra now proceeds in Hebrew, which continues without interruption to the close of the book. A true man of God, he expresses gratitude for answered prayer.
Beautify the house. Ezra’s word of gratitude indicates that Artaxerxes had given authorization for further building activities in connection with the Temple. It is not known whether this work consisted of decorations only or whether it included also buildings. This text doubtless explains why Ezra included Artaxerxes among the kings whose “commandment” caused the Temple to be built (see ch. 9:9, and on ch. 6:14).
27.zh:
以斯拉說：耶和華─我們列祖的神是應當稱頌的！因他使王起這心意修飾耶路撒冷耶和華的殿，

**應當稱頌的。**在引用了亞蘭原文的重要文件之後，以斯拉恢復使用希伯來語，直到本卷的結束，沒有間斷。作為上帝的真僕人，他為祈禱蒙應允而謝恩。
**修飾耶路撒冷耶和華的殿。**以斯拉感恩的話表明亞達薛西已經授權進一步實施聖殿的工程。尚不清楚這是指建殿本身，還是包括裝修在內。這裡無疑解釋了為什麼以斯拉把亞達薛西包括在發令建殿的國王當中（見拉9:9；見拉6:14註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（27–28節）**。《先知與君王》第612頁。

13.en: **All they of the people.** The decree of Artaxerxes is as broad in scope as the proclamation of Cyrus (ch. 1:3), and gives permission not only to the Jews but to all Israelites of every tribe to accompany Ezra to Jerusalem. That Israelites of all the tribes actually went up to Jerusalem on the occasion is implied by the reference to “twelve bullocks for all Israel,” which those who returned with Ezra offered, on their arrival, to the “God of Israel” (see on ch. 8:35).
13.zh:
住在我國中的以色列人、祭司、利未人，凡甘心上耶路撒冷去的，我降旨準他們與你同去。

亞達薛西一世諭旨的範圍與居魯士的一樣大（拉1:3），不僅批准猶太人，也批准許以色列的所有支派隨以斯拉回耶路撒冷。那些隨以斯拉回歸的人在到達的時候，向“以色列的上帝”（見拉8:35註釋），“為以色列眾人獻公牛十二隻”。這說明確有各支派的人回耶路撒冷。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第611頁。

11.en:
**The priest.** The genealogy of vs. 1–5 implies that Ezra was priest, but v. 11 provides the only specific statement of this fact. Nehemiah also so designates Ezra (ch. 8:2, 9).
The scribe. Here for the first time sopher is used in the NT sense of grammateus, “scribe,” meaning a man trained in the exposition of the Scriptures. Ezra stands at the head of a line of famous Hebrew scholars, which in the time of Christ included men like Hillel and Gamaliel, whom the Jews considered worthy successors of Ezra.
11.zh:
祭司以斯拉是通達耶和華誡命和賜以色列之律例的文士。亞達薛西王賜給他們諭旨，上面寫著說：

**祭司。**1-5節的家譜暗示以斯拉是祭司，11節則專門指出這個事實。尼希米也這樣稱呼以斯拉（尼8:2,9）。
**文士。**這是sopher第一次用於新約grammateus（文士）的詞義，指講解聖經的專業人士。以斯拉是最著名的希伯來學者。在基督的時代，猶太人把希列和迦瑪列這樣的人視為以斯拉的繼承者。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《先知與君王》第610頁。

22.en:
**Unto an hundred talents of silver.** According to the weight of the light Babylonian talent, this would be 3,013 kgs., or 3.32 tons. In addition, Ezra could require 100 cor of wheat (22,000 liters, or 624 bu.), and 100 baths (2,200 liters, or 581 gals.) each of wine and oil.
In the Babylonian contract tablets oil and wine are usually dealt with in “jars” whose capacity is not known. Prices for wine varied from one to eight shekels a jar, according to the quality of the wine and the season of the year. Compare Vol. I, p. 169.
A requisition to the treasurer for wheat, wine, oil, and salt seems strange today, but was natural enough in the Persian system, where taxation was partly in kind and every province was required to remit to the royal court the choicest portion of its produce. Wine, corn, oil, and salt were all produced abundantly in Palestine, which was “a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of oil olive and of honey” (2 Kings 18:32), and, in the region about the Dead Sea, abounded with salt.
22.zh:
就是銀子直到一百他連得，麥子一百柯珥，酒一百罷特，油一百罷特，鹽不計其數，也要給他。

**銀子直到一百他連得。**依據巴比倫較輕的衡制，這裡是3,013千克或3.013噸。以斯拉還可以得到100柯珥麥子（22,000公升，或624蒲式耳），酒和油各100罷特（2,200公升，或581加侖）。
在巴比倫合同書板上，油和酒通常以“罐”為交易單位，其容量不明。酒的價格根據質量和季節，為1至8舍客勒一罐。參本書卷一169頁。
向庫官提取小麥，酒，油和鹽，這在今天看來似乎很奇怪，但是在波斯時代是很自然的。因為那時納稅，部分是用實物支付的。而且各省都要把最好的產品上繳朝廷。巴勒斯坦盛產酒、糧、油和鹽。“有糧食和葡萄園之地，有橄欖樹和蜂蜜之地”（王下18:32）。死海周邊地區有豐富的鹽。

21.en:
**All the treasurers.** The “decree” included in Ezra’s authorization was probably sent out separately to the royal treasurer resident in Judea, and to those in the satrap’s office who dealt with the financial matters of that province. It was hardly the intent of Artaxerxes that Ezra should demand the revenue of such provinces as Samaria or Ammon, whose inhabitants were Judea’s enemies. The Aramaic title translated “treasurer” appears also on objects from Persepolis.
Ezra … the scribe. On Ezra’s official title, see on v. 12.
21.zh:
我─亞達薛西王又降旨與河西的一切庫官，說：通達天上神律法的文士祭司以斯拉，無論向你們要什麼，你們要速速地備辦，

**一切庫官。**在授權以斯拉時所提到的這份諭旨，可能另外發給猶大的王室庫官，和該省負責財政事務的官員。亞達薛西似乎不大可能讓以斯拉從撒瑪利亞省或亞捫省的歲收中提款，因為那裡的居民是與猶大人作對的。在波斯波立的文物上，也有亞蘭語的“庫官”稱號。
**文士祭司以斯拉。**關於以斯拉的正式稱呼，見第12註釋。

17.en: **Buy speedily.** Rather, “buy judiciously” or “with all diligence” (RSV). Artaxerxes was not concerned with how soon the money was to be spent, but how well. The primary purpose of the money sent by Ezra was to maintain the Jewish ritual (see ch. 6:9, 10).
17.zh:
所以你當用這金銀，急速買公牛、公綿羊、綿羊羔，和同獻的素祭奠祭之物，獻在耶路撒冷─你們神殿的壇上。

**急速買。**“審慎地買”，“積極地”。亞達薛西自然不是指快把錢花掉，而是怎樣把它花好。以斯拉攜帶這筆金銀的主要目的是要維持猶太人的儀式（見拉6:9,10）。

20.en:
**Whatsoever more.** Here the flexibility of the decree becomes apparent. Ezra is granted unlimited access to the royal revenue of the province of Judea, to be used for any purpose connected with the Temple. Within the limitations stated in v. 22, Ezra’s own discretion was to determine what should be done.
King’s treasure house. Not the royal treasury at Susa or Persepolis, where tribute from the various provinces was stored, but the local treasury of Judea, to which the Jews made their remittances and from which Ezra was now authorized to draw.
20.zh:
你神殿裡若再有需用的經費，你可以從王的府庫裡支取。

**若再有。**這裡表現了諭旨的靈活性。以斯拉可以無限制地使用猶大省的王室府庫，用在與聖殿有關的項目上。在第22節的範圍內，以斯拉有權是自己作出決定。
**王的府庫。**不是存放各省貢物的蘇沙或波斯波立的王室府庫，而是猶大地區的府庫。這是猶太人向其納稅，以斯拉受權可以提取的府庫。

25.en:
**Magistrates and judges.** The closing part of the decree (vs. 25 and 26) authorizes Ezra to reorganize the judicial system of Judea and to be responsible for all future appointments of judicial officers in that province. The word shapheṭin, “magistrates,” is simply the Aramaicized Hebrew equivalent of the word translated “judges.” The word has not been found in non-Jewish documents written in Aramaic, but its root verb appears in Jewish records found at Elephantine. Its use in the decree of Ezra 7 is one more proof that a Hebrew-speaking Jew, probably Ezra, was responsible for the wording of this document.
Beyond the river. See on Ezra 4:10. That Ezra’s jurisdiction was not intended to cover the entire area of “Beyond the River” is evident from the additional explanatory clause, “all such as know the laws of thy God.” It assigns to Ezra’s jurisdiction only the Jewish portion of the population, including Jewish proselytes.
Teach ye them. Ezra, who was probably responsible for the wording of the decree, must have known something about the spiritual conditions prevailing in Judea, which had convinced him of the need for instructing the returned exiles in the law of God. Knowing that his personal conviction on the matter might not carry much weight with the leadership in Judea, he secured royal authorization for this work in order that the Jews might not be tempted to slight this aspect of his program of reform. That the initiative for these provisions in the decree came from Ezra is implied in vs. 6, 28.
25.zh:
以斯拉啊，要照著你神賜你的智慧，將所有明白你神律法的人立為士師、審判官，治理河西的百姓，使他們教訓一切不明白神律法的人。

**士師、審判官。**諭旨的結尾部分（第25節和26節）授權以斯拉重建猶大的司法系統，負責任命該省的司法官員。“士師“（shaphetin）一詞，只見諸於亞蘭語的希伯來文獻。在非猶太人的亞蘭語文獻裡沒有出現。在厄勒番丁島的猶太人文獻中，有該詞的動詞詞根。拉7章的諭旨用了這個詞，進一步證明這個諭旨是一位說希伯來語的猶太人，也許就是以斯拉起草的。
**河西的。**見拉4:10註釋。以斯拉的管轄權並不包括整個“河西”地帶，這一點可以從後面的解釋：“明白上帝律法的人”中看出來。以斯拉只負責管理猶太人，包括接受猶太人信仰的人。
**使他們教訓。**以斯拉可能是諭旨的起草人。他了解猶太人的屬靈狀況。他認為有必要把上帝的律法教誨迴歸的人。他知道單憑他自己的信念，不足以領導猶太人民。所以他爭取了王室在這方面的授權，使猶太人不至於輕視他改革的計劃。第6,28節暗示諭旨中的這些條款出自以斯拉。

1.zh:
這事以後，波斯王亞達薛西年間，有個以斯拉，他是西萊雅的兒子，西萊雅是亞撒利雅的兒子，亞撒利雅是希勒家的兒子，

**這事以後。**作者用一個《以斯拉記》所尚未用過的詞，對本書的兩個部分作了明顯的劃分。第六章和第七章的實際間隔大約有五十八年：從公元前515年的春天（見拉6:15）到公元前457年的年初（見拉7:7）。
**亞達薛西。**關於這個國王名字的拼寫，見第四章補充註釋。本註釋和大多數保守的學者都認為這裡所指的是公元前465-423年當政的亞達薛西一世。關於這一點的證據，見本章補充註釋。
**有個以斯拉，他是西萊雅的兒子。**以斯拉可能是西萊雅的玄孫。聖經作者常稱所有的後代為 “兒子”，所有的祖先為“父親”。基督是“大衛的兒子”，大衛是“亞伯拉罕的兒子”（太1:1原文）。約蘭“生烏西亞（烏西雅）”（太1:8，實際上是他的玄孫。見代上3:11,12）。烏西雅又叫亞撒利雅。以斯拉可能省略了不太出名的父親，祖父和曾祖父，稱自己是所羅門聖殿最後一任大祭司西萊雅的後代（王下25:18）。
西萊雅的父親亞撒利雅，只在代上6:13,14和拉7:1中提到。但是亞撒利雅的父親希勒家無疑是約西亞當政時的大祭司（王下22:4-14；代下34:14-22）。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–28節）**。《先知與君王》第607-614頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第233頁；《先知與君王》第698頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《先知與君王》第608頁。
1.en:
**Now after these things.** The author makes a marked division between the first and second sections of the book by means of an expression used nowhere else in the book of Ezra. The actual time interval between events described in ch. 6 and in ch. 7 seems to have been almost 58 years—from the spring of 515 .. (see ch. 6:15) to the early months of 457 .. (see ch. 7:7).
Artaxerxes. For the spelling of the king’s name see Additional Note on Chapter 4. With the majority of conservative scholars, this commentary holds that the Artaxerxes here mentioned is Artaxerxes Longimanus, who reigned from 465–423 .. For a summary of the evidence in favor of this view, see Additional Note at the close of this chapter.
Ezra the son of Seraiah. Ezra was probably the great-great-grandson of Seraiah. In the language of the Bible writers, every descendant is a “son,” and every ancestor a “father.” Christ is “the son of David,” and David “the son of Abraham” (Matt. 1:1). Joram “begat Ozias [Uzziah]” (Matt. 1:8), his great-great-grandson (see 1 Chron. 3:11, 12, where Uzziah’s other name, Azariah, is used). Ezra probably omits the names of his father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, who were undistinguished, and claims descent from Seraiah, the last high priest to minister in Solomon’s Temple (2 Kings 25:18).
Azariah, the father of Seraiah, is mentioned only in the genealogical list of 1 Chron. 6:13, 14 and in Ezra 7:1, but Azariah’s father Hilkiah is no doubt the high priest of Josiah’s time (2 Kings 22:4–14; 2 Chron. 34:14–22).

5.zh:
布基是亞比書的兒子，亞比書是非尼哈的兒子，非尼哈是以利亞撒的兒子，以利亞撒是大祭司亞倫的兒子。

在第1-5節中，以斯拉追溯蹤了自己的家譜直到第一為大祭司亞倫。參閱代上6:3-15的家譜可以看出，以斯拉在第3節亞撒利雅和米拉約之間省略了六個名字（代上6:7-10），在第2節撒督和亞希突之間省略了米拉約（見代上9:11）。省略次要名字是猶太人家譜的普遍做法。一個顯著的例子是《馬太福音》中耶穌的家譜省略了好幾個名字（見太1:5,11,15,17註釋）。
雖然以斯拉是亞倫的後代，屬於大祭司的家族，但他本人並不是大祭司，而只是一位普通“祭司”（拉7:11,12；尼8:2）。
5.en:
**The son of Aaron.** In vs. 1–5 Ezra traces his genealogy back to Aaron, the first high priest. A comparison with the genealogical list provided in 1 Chron. 6:3–15 shows that Ezra omitted six names between the Azariah and Maraioth of v. 3, which are found in 1 Chron. 6:7–10, and another name (Meraioth) between Zadok and Ahitub of v. 2 (see 1 Chron. 9:11). The abbreviation of genealogies by the omission of unimportant names was a common practice among the Jews. A notable instance is the omission of several names in Matthew’s genealogy of Christ (see on Matt. 1:5, 11, 15, 17).
Although Ezra was a descendant of Aaron, and thus belonged to the high-priestly family, he was not a high priest himself, but only a “priest” (Ezra 7:11, 12; Neh. 8:2).

6.zh:
這以斯拉從巴比倫上來，他是敏捷的文士，通達耶和華─以色列神所賜摩西的律法書。王允准他一切所求的，是因耶和華─他神的手幫助他。

**以斯拉從巴比倫上來。**拉2:1用其中的同一個動詞描述第一批迴歸的被擄者。
**敏捷的。**希伯來語是mahir。該詞在亞蘭語和埃及語中指技術高明，書寫快速的文士。在厄勒番丁島的草紙文獻上，阿希卡用mahir說自己是“一個聰明敏捷的文士”。他希望以此來說明自己不但是文士，而且是有學問的人。在埃及，mahir成為熟練文士的專業稱謂。這樣的人必須在屬世的各方面學問上受過充分的訓練。以斯拉是在宗教方面發揮他的才幹，成為精通“摩西的律法書”的學者。見第11節註釋。
**耶和華以色列上帝。**以斯拉十分虔誠，始終牢記律法不是一個地上立法者所制訂的法典，而是上帝直接的恩賜，是“耶和華的律法”（第10節），“耶和華的誡命，和賜以色列之律例”（第11節）以及“耶和華藉摩西吩咐以色列人的律法”（尼8:14）。
**他一切所求的。**以斯拉給國王留下良好的印象，贏得了他的信任。至於如何達到這一點，我們無從得知。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第609頁。
6.en:
**Ezra went up.** See ch. 2:1, where the same expression, “went up,” is used in regard to the first group of returning exiles.
Ready. Heb. mahir, a word used also in Aramaic and Egyptian to designate a skilled, fast-writing scribe. In the Elephantine papyri Ahikar refers to himself as “a wise and ready scribe,” and uses the same word mahir. He thus wished to indicate that he was not only a scribe but a learned man. In Egypt, where mahir had become a professional title for skilled scribes, such a man was highly trained in every phase of secular learning. Ezra, however, used his talents in the realm of religion, being a scholar “in the law of Moses.” See on v. 11.
Which the Lord God. It is characteristic of Ezra’s piety never to forget that the law was not a mere human code given by an earthly lawgiver, but a direct, divine gift—“the law of the Lord” (v. 10), “the words of the commandments of the Lord, and of his statutes to Israel” (v. 11), and “the law which the Lord had commanded by Moses” (Neh. 8:14).
All his request. Ezra had made a favorable impression on the king and had won his confidence. How this was accomplished is unknown.

7.zh:
亞達薛西王第七年，以色列人、祭司、利未人、歌唱的、守門的、尼提寧，有上耶路撒冷的。

**亞達薛西王第七年。**以斯拉可能按照猶太人的習慣推定亞達薛西王的第七年，即按照始於秋天的猶太人民用歷（見本書卷二，第110,112,138,140頁）。按照本卷第108頁的年表，亞達薛西一世當政的第七年是從公元前458年秋天到公元前457年秋天。關於這些日期以及第8,9節的日期，見本卷第100-103頁的解釋。
**以色列人。**這裡所提隨以斯拉回歸的六種人，上文也提到（拉2:70）隨所羅巴伯迴歸。其列舉的順序基本相同。
7.en:
**The children of Israel.** The same six classes of colonists are here mentioned as returning under Ezra that, according to the earlier narrative (ch. 2:70), had accompanied Zerubbabel. The order of mention is nearly, but not quite, the same.
Seventh year of Artaxerxes. Ezra probably counted the 7th year of Artaxerxes according to the Jewish custom, that is, in terms of the Jewish civil calendar year, which began in the fall (see Vol. II, pp. 110, 112, 138, 140). The 7th regnal year of Artaxerxes I began in the fall of 458 .. and ended in the fall of 457, according to the table on page 108 of this volume. For an explanation of these dates and those of vs. 8, 9, see pp. 100–103 of this volume.

8.zh:
王第七年五月，以斯拉到了耶路撒冷。

第9節告訴我們，以斯拉定於宗教年曆的正月（尼散月）初一出發。這並不奇怪。因為人們通常選擇乾燥的季節進行長達幾個月的行程。同樣，所有的軍事行動也都是在春天開始的。按照本書108頁的猶太人年曆，他們很可能是在公元前457年3月27日出發的。路上花了差不多四個月的時間。這些迴歸者於五月（埃波月）初一日到達耶路撒冷，大約是公元前457年6月23日。以斯拉的人馬花了四個月才到達耶路撒冷，表面上看似乎很久，但不要忘記這樣的隊伍是需要多次休整的。其中有一次據記載是在亞哈瓦河邊（拉8:15）。在居魯斯年輕時代的行軍日誌裡，有一個從以弗所到巴比倫附近庫那克薩的旅途詳細記錄。雖然到達庫那克薩行軍只化了91天，但是整個旅程包括休息的日子，共用了大約半年（色諾芬《遠征記》ii.1.6）。所以以斯拉的旅程化了四個月是不奇怪的。有些耽擱因為旅途的種種危險幾乎是不可避免的（見拉8:31）。關於行軍的可能路線，見拉2:68註釋。
8.en: **He came to Jerusalem.** From v. 9 it appears that the first day of the first month (Nisan) of the religious year had been selected for the beginning of the journey. This is not surprising, since the dry season was usually used for such a journey, one that a caravan required several months to complete. Similarly, all military campaigns were begun in the spring. The day of departure, according to the Jewish calendar on p. 108, was most probably March 27, 457 .. The time occupied on the way was nearly four months. The exiles arrived at Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month (Ab), or approximately July 23, 457 .. That it took Ezra’s group four months to reach Jerusalem seems at first thought a long time, but it should not be forgotten that a caravan like his must have taken a number of prolonged rests, one of which is recorded as occurring at Ahava (ch. 8:15). The log of the march of the army of the younger Cyrus from Ephesus to Cunaxa near Babylon provides an actual record of such a journey. Although Cunaxa was reached in 91 marching days, the entire journey, including resting days, occupied about half a year (Xenophon Anabasis ii. 1. 6). We need not be surprised, therefore, that Ezra’s journey occupied four months. Some delay must almost certainly have been occasioned by the perils of the trek (see ch. 8:31). As to the probable route, see on ch. 2:68.

9.zh:
正月初一日，他從巴比倫起程；因他神施恩的手幫助他，五月初一日就到了耶路撒冷。

這裡所提到上帝的特別恩典可能包括國王對以斯拉請求的回應（見第6節），以及脫離想在路上襲擊隊伍的敵人（見拉8:21-23,31）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《歷代願望》第233頁；《先知與君王》第611,617,698頁。
9.en: **The good hand.** The special divine favor here referred to probably includes the royal response to Ezra’s request (see v. 6), and deliverance from enemies who had intended to attack the caravan on the way (see ch. 8:21–23, 31).

10.zh:
以斯拉定志考究遵行耶和華的律法，又將律例典章教訓以色列人。

以斯拉是一個獻身的人。他的人生目標和志向就是認識上帝的旨意，與上帝合作，並教導他人也這樣做。上帝現在也呼召這樣的人去從事特別的工作。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第608,623頁。
10.en: **Prepared his heart.** Ezra was a consecrated man. The aim and ambition of his life was to know the will of God, to cooperate with God, and to teach others to do likewise. This was the man God now called to do a special work.

28.zh:
又在王和謀士，並大能的軍長面前施恩於我。因耶和華─我神的手幫助我，我就得以堅強，從以色列中招聚首領，與我一同上來。

**施恩於我。**許多現代註釋家認為，在《以斯拉記》中，只有用第一人稱單數的口吻所寫的部分才出於以斯拉的筆下，其他用第三人稱單數指以斯拉的部分是被別人寫的（見拉7:1-11；10:1）。我們如果認真研究古代文獻，就可以知道，人稱的轉換並不一定證明作者的改變。在埃及語（辛奴亥故事，見出2:15註釋），亞述語（薩爾貢二世編年史），亞爛語（亞卡的故事），希伯來語（但4章）和希臘語（修西戴狄斯）的文獻中，有許多這樣的例子。這些著作有相同的特徵。即使在一些現代的文學作品裡，也有作家從第一人稱一下子轉到第三人稱，或從第三人稱轉到第一人稱，如凱特爾所做的那樣。
**在王……面前。**見第15節的註釋。這裡進一步證明以斯拉是作為一個請願者出現在亞達薛西和他的內閣面前的（又見第6節）。雖然以斯拉的成功，特別是在獲得諭旨的事上，在很大的程度上是因為他的聰明和智慧，但其實是天意的手在一步一步引導他。所以他自然承認他的成功是因為上帝的良善。是上帝在他面前的國王和官長心中做工。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第614頁。
28.en:
**Unto me.** Many modern commentators have thought that only those parts of the book of Ezra which are written in the first person singular can be attributed to Ezra, and that those parts which refer to Ezra in the third person singular were written by someone else (see chs. 7:1–11; 10:1). However, a careful study of ancient documents shows that a change of pronouns is no proof of a change in authorship. Examples can be given from Egyptian (the Sinuhe story, see on Ex. 2:15), Assyrian (Annals of Sargon II), Aramaic (Ahikar story), Hebrew (Dan. 4), and Greek (Thucydides) documents, in which the same peculiarity appears. Even in some modern literary works writers change suddenly from the first to the third person or vice versa, as Kittel has shown.
Before the king. See on v. 15. Here is further evidence that Ezra had appeared before Artaxerxes and his cabinet as a petitioner (see also v. 6). Although it must be assumed that Ezra’s tact and wisdom were responsible for much of the success that crowned his efforts, especially in obtaining the decree, the hand of Providence led him on step by step. He freely acknowledged that his success was due to God’s goodness and that God had worked on the hearts of the king and the rulers before whom he had appeared.

900.zh:
在第十九世紀末以前，猶太人和基督徒都認為《以斯拉記》裡的亞達薛西就是在波斯國的第一個國王。希臘語叫亞達薛西·朗吉馬納斯（Longimanus，意為“長手”），執政時間是公元前465年到423年。但自從1890年起，這種看法有了很大的變化。當時比利時學者A.Van Hoonacker（胡納克）發表了他有關以斯拉和尼希米年代的第一篇論文，主張要改變傳統的排序，試圖把以斯拉說成是尼希米的繼承者。他的觀點在學術界贏得了許多追隨者。主張改變傳統排序的人數和持傳統看法的人數大致相等。由於這個問題的重要性，特別是關但9:24-27預言，及其準確的日期，本文就該問題進行詳細分析。
認為以斯拉是尼希米繼承者的學者分為兩種：一種認為《以斯拉記》第七章的事件發生在亞達薛西一世執政的最後一年，也就是第三十七年（公元前427年），而不是聖經所說的第七年；另一種認為以斯拉的迴歸是在亞達薛西二世第七年（公元前405/04年-359/58年）。
第一種看法這裡不予探討，因為它純屬推測，不接受拉7章的日期，而另定一個日期。認為以斯拉在耶路撒冷活動遲於尼希米的大多數學者都接受這種看法。
持第二看法的學者所提出的理由比較有力。他們指出聖經並沒有說明拉7章裡的亞達薛西是三個亞達薛西中的哪一個。他們把拉7章和8章的事件定在亞達薛西二世七年，而不是亞達薛西一世七年，並沒有與聖經的記錄衝突。每一個研究聖經的人都承認聖經對事件的記錄不一定是按照年代排列的。所以不能排斥認為拉7-10章的時間是在《尼希米記》事件以後的觀點。
首先要了解為什麼學者們會放棄傳統的立場，即以斯拉到耶路撒冷是在亞達薛西一世七年，尼希米到耶路撒冷則是在亞達薛西一世二十年。在主張顛倒傳統排序的許多理由中只有下面五點有一定意義：
一、尼希米不太瞭解以斯拉。如果按照拉7章的描述，以斯拉到耶路撒冷時享有很大的行政，宗教和司法權利的話，為什麼他沒有在尼希米的時代發揮更大的作用？尼8:1-6,9確實提到以斯拉是宣讀律法書的人（尼8:1-6,9），和奉獻城牆時兩個歌詠隊伍的領隊之一（尼12:36），但他的活動與尼希米的完全無法相比。在另一方面，如果他在尼希米時代只是一個比較年輕的亞倫譜系的祭司，只讓他宣讀律法，而沒有擔任行政要職就是很自然的了。可以假定他後來受到波斯國王的重視，被派往猶大，享有拉7章所描寫的廣泛權力。
二、尼希米沒有提隨以斯拉回歸的人。尼希米在重新安排耶路撒冷的人口時，統計了差不多一個世紀以前隨所羅巴伯迴歸的各支派名冊（尼7章），似乎完全忽略了十三年前隨以斯拉回歸的人（據拉7章和8章，假定迴歸是在公元前457年）。但如果以斯拉率領五六千人迴歸是在亞達薛西二世當政時的話，尼希米重新安置人口所依據的名冊，就只能是所羅巴伯的那一份。
三、以斯拉找到了尼希米所任命的小組。以斯拉到達耶路撒冷時，把亞達薛西交給他財寶託付給四個利未人。他們顯然是負責管理聖殿基金的（拉8:33）。尼希米報導說，在他第二次任職期間，曾任命了一個四人小組管理庫房（尼13:13）。這說明這個小組在他以前並不存在。從而可以得出結論：以斯拉肯定在這個小組設立以後才到耶路撒冷的，也就是在尼希米第一次擔任省長以後。
四、城牆是在以斯拉到達之前竣工的。以斯拉曾為顯然竣工不久的“在猶大和耶路撒冷有牆垣”（拉9:9）而感謝上帝。但尼希米所見到的只是廢墟，並不得不在他到達耶路撒冷的第一年重建城牆。
五、大祭司約哈難屬於下一代人。約哈難常常被引用作為以斯拉遲於尼希米的主要證據。以利亞實的兒子約哈難是尼12:22,23所提到的最後族長或大祭司之一。由於以利亞實是尼希米當省長時的大祭司（尼3:1,20,21；13:4,7），約哈難要麼是他的兒子，要麼是他的孫子（在尼12:12中，以利亞實和約哈難之間有耶何耶大），他是屬於下一代的人。這個結論與猶太人文獻所提到約哈難是公元前410年的大祭司一致的。在厄勒番丁島的草紙文稿中（見本書第79-83頁），有一封寫於公元前407年11月25日（按照波斯年曆）的信函，是寫給波斯的猶大省長比革瓦伊的。信中說作者們曾在三年前寫信給“大祭司約哈難，和他在耶路撒冷的祭司同事”（考利版，第30號）。
此外，以斯拉到達耶路撒冷時，以利亞實的兒子約哈難在聖殿裡有一個房間（拉10:6）。如果以斯拉到達耶路撒冷是公元前457年，看到約哈難在聖殿裡有一個房間，那麼，擔任祭司的約哈難至少已有二十歲了（見拉3:8），或者要大得多。如果按草紙文獻所提示，約哈難在公元前410年擔任大祭司，他那時一定至少67歲。由於他的繼承者押杜亞（尼12:11,22）在78年以後亞歷山大大帝經過巴勒斯坦時擔任大祭司（公元前332年，見約瑟弗斯《上古史》xi.8.4,5），押杜亞那時一定有一百來歲了。
那些認為尼希米比以斯拉早的人說，如果假定以斯拉是在亞達薛西二世時到達耶路撒冷（公元前405/04-359/58年）的，那就可以解決押杜亞在100歲擔任大祭司的難題。這樣就就可以說，約哈難在公元前410年之前不久接續尼希米的同時代人、以利亞實的兒子耶何耶大擔任大祭司。假定約哈難在公元前410年時約三十歲，那麼以斯拉於亞達薛西二世執政第七年到達耶路撒冷時，他會是43歲，在聖殿有一個房間可供以斯拉使用（拉10:6）。如果我們進一步假定押杜亞生於約哈難中年之後，比如說40歲的時候，那麼在亞歷山大到來時他大約七十歲。
以上是學者們所提出改變以斯拉和尼希米前往耶路撒冷傳統排序的五點最重要的論據。現在根據傳統的以斯拉-尼希米排序來考慮這些論據。
一.  以斯拉在尼希米的時代是平民身份。以斯拉在公元前457年到達耶路撒冷時擁有很大的權力，但不如十三年以後擔任省長的尼希米。以斯拉曾得到國王的寵愛，受權返回猶大按照猶太律法恢復司法系統（見拉7:26）。他還獲得大筆撥款，受權加強城市的防禦。在猶大省所屬的“河西的總督”麥迦比佐斯反叛期間（見本書第62頁），撒瑪利亞人乘機直接上書國王，向國王保證他們的忠誠，同時指控猶太人重建城牆是居心叵測。優柔寡斷，慣於投機的亞達薛西，聽到撒瑪利亞人的表白，可能十分高興，並希望他們的忠誠會給在反叛的麥迦比佐斯轄地裡製造困難，於是就准許撒瑪利亞人去阻止重建耶路撒冷的城牆。但撒瑪利亞人並不滿足於僅僅阻止猶太人的工程。他們可能還拆毀了部分城牆，燒燬了幾個城門（見尼1:3註釋）。
亞達薛西與麥迦比佐斯和解以後，恢復了與“河西”地區的正常關係。尼希米從他的兄弟那裡（見尼1:2註釋）聽到了猶大省在分開期間所發生的事情。於是尼希米請求寵愛他的國王派他帶著重建城牆的充分授權回到耶路撒冷去（尼1章和2章）。
儘管尼希米擁有重建城牆的充分授權，但他到達耶路撒冷以後還是非常審慎，因為他完全知道敵人的勢力和頑固。他最初行動的機密（尼2:12-16），以及他後來應付阻撓的決心，證明他有充分的資格完成以斯拉曾經從事卻受到阻止的任務。
因此以斯拉可能認為自己站在背後，直到城牆竣工乃是聰明之舉。以斯拉也可能一直受到敵人的指控，因為他回到耶路撒冷時趕走了猶太人家庭中的外邦妻子（拉9章和10章）。也許是出於審慎，尼希米在開始時表面上沒有與以斯拉發生什麼聯繫。
但既然城牆即已竣工，就沒有什麼顧忌的了。尼希米在國家事務上自然會賦予以斯拉合適的位置。在奉獻城牆的典禮上，他請以斯拉率領兩個歌詠隊中的一個，他自己則率領另一個隊（尼12:36,38）。這兩支隊伍必須由在重建城牆的工程中做出過傑出貢獻的人來率領。
後來到了節期來到的時候，以斯拉無可爭議地成為宗教的領袖，指導百姓的活動（尼8:1-6,9,13）。這說明尼希米沒有忽視以斯拉，而是在時機成熟的時候給予他合適的位置。那種認為在《尼希米記》第八章至第十二章中沒有以斯拉的名字，因此他就無足輕重的看法是不正確的。若是這樣，那麼奉獻城牆典禮中兩支隊伍中，有一支隊伍就沒有領導者了。把以斯拉解釋為先是尼希米的先驅者，後是他的合作者，完全符合已知的事實。
二. 尼希米採用的是最早的人口普查表。尼希米採用所羅巴伯時代的人口普查表，作為他重新安排耶路撒冷人口的基礎（尼7章），並不意味著他忽視那些最近隨以斯拉回來的人和還沒有回來的人。我們對於那段時期的事件知之甚少。跟隨以斯拉回來的人可能比隨所羅巴回來的人更願意住在耶路撒冷，所以尼希米只好查閱一下更早的人口普查表。查閱最早普查表的另一個原因可能是隨所羅巴伯回來的50,000人，比起隨以斯拉到達耶路撒冷的較少人口，更加均勻地分佈在全家各地。由於所羅巴伯的普查表不包括僕人和藝人就有四十五批人，而以斯拉的統計表上只有十八批人，前一份普查表顯然更具代表性。《尼希米記》第七章沒有提到以斯拉的普查表，不能證明它在尼希米的時代是不存在的。
三. 庫官的職務不是最先由尼希米設立的。不要以為尼希米在第二次擔任省長時，才第一次任命了庫官。尼13:10-14的記錄說的是尼希米第二次到達耶路撒冷時，發現百姓好久沒有繳納什一，聖殿的員工為了生計只得耕種土地。尼希米回來以後立刻糾正這種局面。他說服猶太人重新繳納什一，並把利未人和歌手召回聖殿。由於需要庫官來管理資金，他就指定了四個人。拉8:33提到四名庫官，並不意味著所有的聖殿基金都必須由四人小組來管理。說這樣的職務在尼希米第二個任期以前不存在，是沒有事實根據的。
四. 以斯拉為準許建築城牆而感謝上帝。如果上述第一點中對以斯拉活動的歸納符合歷史事實的話，以斯拉在公元前457年迴歸時是得到重建耶路撒冷城牆的授權的。所以他向上帝感恩也就不足為奇了（拉9:9）。是祂感動波斯國王（居魯士和亞達薛西一世）使以色列“復興”，支持以色列人建造他們上帝的殿（居魯士和大流士一世）；使他們“在猶大和耶路撒冷有牆垣”（亞達薛西一世）。值得注意的是以斯拉並沒有說城牆已經竣工。除非還有其他的證據證明城牆在他禱告之前已經完工。但單憑祈禱本身，只能理解為上帝的恩典准許重建城牆工程的進行，不是說城牆已經竣工，也不能證明《以斯拉書》第九章和十章所描述的改革發生在《尼希米記》的事件之後。
五. 約哈難的年齡並不是異常的。沒有理由懷疑厄勒番丁島猶太人文獻裡所提到在公元前410年擔任大祭司的約哈難，不是尼12:22,23以利亞實的兒子約哈難。很有可能以斯拉在他的房間裡哭泣過（拉10:6）。即使在公元前457年以斯拉回到耶路撒冷的時候，約哈難已經是受人尊敬的祭司，已達三十來歲，在聖殿有自己的房間，到了公元前410年他依然可以是大祭司，年齡在七八十歲之間，上述厄勒番丁島猶太人的信函就是寫給他的。
這種解釋的唯一難點與押杜亞他關，如果他像約瑟弗斯所說的，是接續約哈難擔任大祭司，並在厄勒番丁島給約哈難的信件七十五年以後，在亞歷山大時代依然任職的話（《上古史》xi.8.4,5）。但這個問題並沒有表面看來那麼困難。即使約瑟弗斯所說亞歷山大時代的大祭司是押杜亞是正確的，也沒有證據證明他就是尼12:11,22的那個押杜亞。在《尼希米記》中還有一個押杜亞，是尼希米時代簽名的一位家長（尼10:21）。所以尼12:11,22中接續約哈難擔任大祭司的押杜亞，可能就是亞歷山大來訪時在聖殿中任職的名叫押杜亞的大祭司的祖父。
應該記住，歷史學家約瑟弗斯在描寫這段時期的歷史時，至少犯了一個嚴重的錯誤，因為他把參巴拉說成是亞歷山大的同時代人（《上古史》xi.8.2,3）。我們從聖經和厄勒番丁島發現的當時文獻中得知，參巴拉是尼希米時代的人。
約瑟弗斯很有可能把猶太人大祭司的名字弄錯了。但亞歷山大訪問耶路撒冷的故事並不一定是杜撰的。
綜上所述，認為以斯拉遲於尼希米的理由是不充分的。所以許多學者不贊成顛倒傳統的排序。況且改變順序說的倡導者同樣也捲入他們想要規避的一些難題。這可以從下面兩點中看出來。
一. 米利末的年齡。公元前457年以斯拉到達耶路撒冷的時候，把從巴比倫所帶來的金銀財寶交給了烏利亞的兒子祭司米利末（拉8:33）。十三年後又提到這個米利末，是尼希米的積極支持者和兩段城牆的熱心建造者（尼3:4,21）。在上述經文中，同一個人從公元前457年到公元前444年期間做了不同的事情，這並沒有什麼問題。
但如果說以斯拉到達耶路撒冷是在公元前397年，即亞達薛西二世七年，那麼從以斯拉手中接收財寶的米利末年紀就十分老邁了。即使米利末是在二十五歲的時候負責建造兩段城牆，他在以斯拉回來時擔任庫官的年齡也已達七十二歲。儘管存在這種可能性，但值得注意的是，新理論自動把米利末的年齡定在其倡導者認為對於約哈難是不可能的年齡上。
還要記住，在以斯拉和尼希米時代，大祭司的職務是終生的。故可以推定他們結束服務的時候，均年事已高。所以亞倫擔任大祭司到123歲；以利到98歲；耶何耶大到130歲（民33:39；撒上4:15；代下24:15）。
二. 以斯拉的年齡。主張改變順序的人，如果認為以斯拉到達耶路撒冷比尼希米遲四十七年，他們在有關他年齡的問題上就遇到了更大的難題。新理論的提倡者都認定以斯拉在尼8章所描寫的活動是中是偉大的宗教領袖，並且擔任城牆奉獻典禮中的兩位領導人之一。但被挑選領導這些活動的人，不是大祭司，就一定是非常有影響的傑出人士，不可能是年輕人。難以想象被選擇擔任這種工作的人小於四十歲。尼希米選擇他，不會不因為他此前所取得的重大成就。但如果推定他是四十七年以後、公元前397年從巴比倫回來的，要讓他在尼希米時代達到有令人尊重的年齡，那將是非常荒謬的。
許多主張改變聖經中以斯拉和尼希米順序的學者意識到這個難點。他們要麼在尼希米的活動中刪去以斯拉的名字，要麼主觀地把他回耶路撒冷的時間定在亞達薛西一世第三十七年。本註釋的讀者可以看出，這兩種主張都改動了聖經。審慎的聖經學者認為沒有理由改變聖經中以斯拉和尼希米到達耶路撒冷的順序。這種改變非但不能解決他們想要解決的難點，而且會製造新的難點，使那段歷史的結構變得非常複雜。我們不能忽視聖經的話語和已知的史實。
