Excavations of Nippur have brought to light numerous documents that show that many wealthy Jews lived in that region of Mesopotamia during the reign of Artaxerxes I. Hence, it may have been a difficult task for Ezra and his fellow leaders to convince as many to return as did accompany him. These returning colonists could expect only a hard pioneering life in the old homeland, with far fewer comforts than in Babylonia. In view of these considerations it is surprising to find that Ezra succeeded in persuading almost 2,000 families to cast in their lot with their brethren in the old homeland.

2.zh:
屬非尼哈的子孫有革順；屬以他瑪的子孫有但以理；屬大衛的子孫有哈突；

**子孫。**第2節列出兩個祭司家族，一個大衛家族。沒有提供各家族的人數，就像第3節的第一個家族（原文）。這些數字在早期抄本中可能就已缺失。故無法算出迴歸者的準確人數。
**哈突。**英文KJV版的標點模糊了革順是非尼哈的兒子、但以理是以他瑪的兒子等事實。在KJV版問世時，分號比冒號表示更長的間隔，現在的情況正好相反。哈突是的大衛的後裔，也是示迦尼的孫子（第3節），這可以從代上3:22,23看出。第2節應該以示迦尼結尾，而不是以哈突的名字結尾。
2.en:
**Of the sons.** In v. 2 two priestly families, and one, of the house of David, are mentioned. The number of men belonging to each of the three families is not given, as is also true of the first family mentioned in v. 3. These numbers may have dropped out in an early copy of the list. Thus it is impossible to give the exact number of returning exiles.
Hattush. The punctuation of the KJV obscures the fact that Gershom was a son of Phinehas, Daniel of Ithamar, etc. At the time the KJV was translated the semicolon represented a greater break than a colon; the reverse is now true. Furthermore, though a remote descendant of David, Hattush was a grandson of Shechaniah (v. 3), as is evident from 1 Chron. 3:22, 23. Verse 2 should close with the name Shechaniah, not with Hattush.

3.zh:
屬巴錄的後裔，就是示迦尼的子孫有撒迦利亞，同著他，按家譜計算，男丁一百五十人；

**巴錄。**這個名字和以後幾節的名字在所羅巴伯時代的名單裡也有提到。見第2章註釋。
3.en: **Pharosh.** For this name and those of the following verses also mentioned in the list of Zerubbabel’s time, see on ch. 2.

5.zh:
屬示迦尼的子孫有雅哈悉的兒子，同著他有男丁三百；

**示迦尼。**在抄寫中漏了一個名字，可能在“子孫”和“示迦尼”之間，或在“示迦尼”和“雅哈悉的兒子”之間。希臘語七十士譯本為“薩土的子孫示迦尼，是雅哈悉的兒子”。薩土在拉2:8中有提到。
5.en: **Shechaniah.** A name has been lost in copying, either between the words “of the sons” and “of Shechaniah,” or between “Shechaniah” and “the son of Jahaziel.” The LXX supports the reading, “Of the sons of Zattu, Shechaniah, the son of Jahaziel.” Zattu is mentioned in ch. 2:8.

10.zh:
屬示羅密的子孫有約細斐的兒子，同著他有男丁一百六十；

**示羅密。**和第5節一樣，這裡似乎也有缺失的名字。七十士譯本為“巴尼的子孫示羅密，是約細斐的兒子”。巴尼在拉2:10中為一個家族的族長。
10.en: **Shelomith.** As in v. 5 there seems to be an omission of a name, which the LXX supplies by reading, “Of the sons of Bani, Shelomith, the son of Josephiah.” Bani appears as the head of a family in ch. 2:10.

13.zh:
屬亞多尼乾的子孫，就是末尾的，他們的名字是以利法列、耶利、示瑪雅，同著他們有男丁六十；

**子孫，就是末尾的。**可能指亞多尼乾的小兒子。年齡大的兒子們似乎已在所羅巴伯的時代回去（拉2:13）。英文RSV版為“後來的人”。
13.en: **The last sons.** Probably the younger sons of Adonikam are meant. The families of the older sons seem to have returned already in Zerubbabel’s time (ch. 2:13). The RSV reads, “those who came later.”

15.zh:
我招聚這些人在流入亞哈瓦的河邊，我們在那裡住了三日。我查看百姓和祭司，見沒有利未人在那裡，

**亞哈瓦的河邊。**見第21節和31節，別處沒有提到。以斯拉的記錄給人的印象是它可能位於巴比倫的腹地，容易接觸到利未人，在那裡對利未人再次發出呼籲（見第15-20節）。有人認為它是《塔木德》裡位於巴比倫西北的'Ihi，即現代的Hît。
**利未人。**利未人少的原因可能與拉2:40相同。那時迴歸的利未人也很少（見拉8:1註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（15–36節）**。《先知與君王》第612-619頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第612頁。
15.en:
**The river.** The river, or canal, called Ahava in vs. 21, 31, is otherwise unknown. The Ezra record leaves the impression that it was rather centrally located in Babylonia, for it was easy to make contact with the Levites, to whom an additional appeal was sent from that place (see vs. 15–20). Some have considered it equivalent to the Talmudic ’Ihi, which they identify with the modern Hît, northwest of Babylon.
Sons of Levi. The reason for the absence of Levites is probably the same as that discussed in connection with ch. 2:40, where the small number of returning Levites is apparent (see also on ch. 8:1).

16.zh:
就召首領以利以謝、亞列、示瑪雅、以利拿單、雅立、以利拿單、拿單、撒迦利亞、米書蘭，又召教習約雅立和以利拿單。

以斯拉似乎因利未人沒有回應他的呼籲而感到吃驚和不安。沒有利未人，他的隊伍就不完整，特別是鑑於他復興的理想（見拉7:10,14-28；參拉9,10章）。除了九個族長以外，他還派“教習” （即18節中的“通達人”），去向利未人發出最後緊急呼籲，為了讓他們加入迴歸的隊伍。這是很有意義的。這兩個人雖然他們沒有正式的稱號，但是他們要麼特別能言善辯，說服力強，要麼在其他方面特別有資格擔任這個任務。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第614頁。
16.en: **Then I sent.** The text seems to indicate that Ezra was not only surprised but perturbed that no Levites had responded to his appeal. Without them his caravan seemed incomplete, particularly in view of his desire to bring about a revival (see ch. 7:10, 14–28; cf. chs. 9, 10). That he sent “men of understanding” in addition to the nine family heads mentioned, to make a last and urgent appeal to the Levites for participation in the return journey, is significant. These two men, although they had no official title or function, were either especially eloquent or persuasive, or were considered otherwise exceptionally qualified for the task at hand.

17.zh:
我打發他們往迦西斐雅地方去見那裡的首領易多，又告訴他們當向易多和他的弟兄尼提寧說什麼話，叫他們為我們神的殿帶使用的人來。

**迦西斐雅。**位置不詳。有人認為這是在巴比倫的猶太人宗教中心，還有人認為這是一所學校的所在地。有年輕的利未人在其中接受教育成為會堂學校的教師。順便提一下，這個利未人中心部落的首領易多，屬於聖殿服務中職務較低的尼提寧人（見拉2:43註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–22節）**。《先知與君王》第615頁。
17.en: **Casiphia.** The location of this place is unknown. Some have suggested that it was a religious center of the Babylonian Jewry, others that a school was located there where young Levites were trained as teachers for the schools of the synagogues. It is worthy of notice, in passing, that Iddo, the village head of this center of Levites, belonged to the technically inferior group of Temple servants called Nethinims (see on ch. 2:43).

18.zh:
蒙我們神施恩的手幫助我們，他們在以色列的曾孫、利未的孫子、抹利的後裔中帶一個通達人來；還有示利比和他的眾子與弟兄共一十八人。

**施恩的手。**這是以斯拉承認上帝引導的常用語氣（見拉7:6,9,28；8:31）。《尼希米記》裡也有相似的說法（尼2:8,18）。但在其他經文中沒有。
**通達人。**希伯來語是'ish sekel，有些註釋家認為的是一個人名，但沒有充足的理由。至今還沒有看到過這個名字。如果把'ish sekel 理解為一個人名，那就面臨更大的困難。因為我們必須假定這份名單缺失了他祖先的名字，以及該利未人家族的人數。這個審慎通達的人，名叫示利比。作為一名利未人的首領，他在尼希米的時代裡不止被提到一次（尼8:7；9:4,5）。
**還有示利比。**希伯來語的連詞we（“還有”），應該譯為“就是”（英文RSV版）。這句就譯成了“帶一個通達人來，就是示利比”。
18.en:
**By the good hand.** This is Ezra’s usual mode of acknowledging divine providence (see chs. 7:6, 9, 28; 8:31). Similar expressions also occur in Nehemiah (ch. 2:8, 18), but not elsewhere in Scripture.
A man of understanding. Heb. ’ish śekel, considered by some commentators as a proper name, but without sufficient reason. No such name is known to have existed. If ’ish śekel is taken as a proper name we are confronted with the further difficulty of having to assume that the name of his ancestors and the number of Levites in his family group have been lost from the list. The name of this man of discretion or prudence is given as Sherebiah, who is mentioned more than once in Nehemiah’s time as a chief Levite (Neh. 8:7; 9:4, 5).
And Sherebiah. The Hebrew conjunction we, “and,” should be rendered “namely” (RSV) or “even,” so that the text reads, “they brought us a man of understanding, … namely Sherebiah.”

20.zh:
從前大衛和眾首領派尼提寧服事利未人，現在從這尼提寧中也帶了二百二十人來，都是按名指定的。

**大衛和眾首領。**《列王記》和《歷代志》裡都沒有提大衛增加聖殿僕役的數量。但這種安排和他所做的其他安排是一致的。最早的尼提寧人可能是基遍人（見書9:21；拉2:43註釋）。
**按名派定的人。**作者顯然認為有必要說明易多已向以斯拉遞交了這些尼提寧人的名單或證書。但他認為不必在敘述中插入這個名單。
20.en:
**David and the princes.** There is no record in either Kings or Chronicles of David’s increasing the number of Temple servants, though such an arrangement accords well with other arrangements he is known to have made. The original Nethinims were probably the Gibeonites (see on Joshua 9:21; Ezra 2:43).
Expressed by name. The narrator evidently considered it necessary to state that a list of names of these Nethinims had been forwarded by Iddo to Ezra, probably by way of credentials, but he does not consider it necessary to insert the list in this account.

21.zh:
那時，我在亞哈瓦河邊宣告禁食，為要在我們神面前克苦己心，求他使我們和婦人孩子，並一切所有的，都得平坦的道路。

**我在亞哈瓦河邊宣告禁食。**禁食通常象徵懺悔，往往與發生過的或可能發生的災難有關。但這次所涉及的是祈求旅途平安。如21和22節所示，要把幾千百姓安全地帶到猶大，以斯拉肩上的責任重大。大隊人馬最大的需要就是求上帝一路保佑。為了讓國王相信真神的大能，以斯拉沒有請求軍隊的護送，或謝絕了這樣的護送（第22節）。尼希米則毫不猶豫地接受途中的護送（尼2:9）。因為在充滿危險，人跡罕至的地帶進行長途跋涉，軍隊護送並不是多餘的奢侈。以斯拉充分意識到這群赤手空拳的迴歸者和數額龐大的財寶所面臨的危險。他知道他們最大的需要就是上帝的保佑，也知道只有百姓和上帝之間沒有罪惡阻隔，上帝才與他們同在。他命令他們禁食和“克苦己心”，是為了讓他們在動身前往猶大以前，能省察自己的生活，併除去一切已知的罪惡。
**婦人孩子。**這說明在以斯拉的時代，所有的男人都是拖家帶口的。而在所羅巴伯的時代，大多數家屬是過一段時間才過來的（見拉2:64註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–23節）**。《先知與君王》第616頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–23節）**。《先知與君王》第619頁；《證言》卷一第282頁。
21.en:
**I proclaimed a fast.** Fasting was usually symbolic of repentance, and often accompanied a disaster that had occurred or was expected. In this case, however, it was held in connection with prayer for a safe journey. The great responsibility of bringing these thousands of people safely to Judea rested heavily on Ezra, as vs. 21 and 22 indicate. The urgent need of the expedition for divine protection on the way was especially real to the members of the caravan, because Ezra, who desired to convince the king of the power of the true God, either had not asked for an armed escort or had declined to accept one (v. 22). Nehemiah, however, had no scruples about traveling with an escort (Neh. 2:9), which was no unnecessary luxury on so dangerous a journey through long stretches of sparsely populated territory. Ezra was fully aware of the existing dangers that confronted a group of unarmed exiles and their great quantity of treasure. Knowing that they needed divine protection more than anything else, but knowing also that God’s presence would be assured only if no sin stood between the people and their God, he ordered them to fast and “afflict” (humble) themselves, meaning that they should search their lives and remove every known sin before setting forward on their way to Judea.
Our little ones. This shows that in Ezra’s time all the men were accompanied by their families, while in Zerubbabel’s time most families had remained behind for a time (see on Ezra 2:64).

22.zh:
我求王撥步兵馬兵幫助我們抵擋路上的仇敵，本以為羞恥；因我曾對王說：我們神施恩的手必幫助一切尋求他的；但他的能力和忿怒必攻擊一切離棄他的。

**路上的仇敵。**見21節註釋。第31節暗示這裡的仇敵是真實存在的。以斯拉可能知道撒瑪利亞人等著要截擊他們的隊伍。一些不效忠波斯的阿拉伯部落聽到消息以後，正準備伏擊和掠奪他們。
22.en: **The enemy in the way.** See on v. 21. Verse 31 implies that no imaginary foe is referred to here. It may be Ezra knew that the Samaritans were waiting to intercept the caravan, or that some of the Arab tribes, who owed no allegiance to Persia, had learned of the caravan and were planning to attack it from ambush and plunder it.

24.zh:
我分派祭司長十二人，就是示利比、哈沙比雅，和他們的弟兄十人，

**示利比、哈沙比雅。**這些人和他們的十個同事都是利未人，但英譯本暗示他們還不是祭司（第18,19節）。七十士譯本把“就是”譯為“以及”，也就是以斯拉任命了十二個祭司長，以及十二個利未人，就是示利比，哈沙比雅和他們的同事，總共二十四人，負責財寶的安全運輸。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–29節）**。《先知與君王》第616頁。
24.en: **Sherebiah, Hashabiah.** These men and their ten associates were Levites, but not priests as the English translation implies (vs. 18, 19). Preceding “Sherebiah” is the preposition le. This is not translated in the KJV. The LXX here reads “and.” Thus translated, the meaning of the passage would be that Ezra appointed 12 chief priests, and in addition to them 12 Levites, namely, Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their colleagues—a total of 24 men—to be responsible for the safe transmission of the treasures.

25.zh:
將王和謀士、軍長，並在那裡的以色列眾人為我們神殿所獻的金銀和器皿，都秤了交給他們。

銀金都是條狀或塊狀的，並不是硬幣。波斯人這時已經使用貨幣，但國庫的儲備都是條狀的（希羅多德iii.96）。
25.en: **Weighed unto them.** The silver and gold were in bars or ingots, not in coined money. The Persians used coined money at this time, but the treasury kept the bulk of its stores in bars (Herodotus iii. 96).

26.zh:
我秤了交在他們手中的銀子有六百五十他連得；銀器重一百他連得；金子一百他連得；

用現代的標準來衡量這裡所列的金銀銅器，是無法體現它們當時的購買力的。根據這三種金屬的重量大體估算其總價值，可能會超過三百萬美元。即使是挑剔的學者也認為這裡所詳細列出的財寶和隨以斯拉回來的家長名單是真實的。如果《以斯拉記》是虛構的，作者就不必用這麼多的篇幅來列舉迴歸者的名單，並詳細說明財寶的內容。
財寶中相當大一部分可能來自國庫，但有不少是住在波斯和巴比倫的猶太富人以及他們的外邦朋友所捐獻的（見拉7:15,16）。儘管帶回猶大的財寶似乎很多，但不要忘記波斯帝國當時是非常富裕的（見但11:2）。希羅多德說（iii.94,95），印度每年上繳了360他連得金沙（13.5短噸，即12.3公噸），巴比倫上繳1,000他連得銀子（37.7短噸，即34.3公噸）。其他省份上繳的數量也很可觀。希羅多德說帝國的歲收是14,560埃維厄他連得。一些註釋家認為，與這麼龐大的總額相比，以斯拉帶回猶大的財寶並不算多。
26.en:
**Silver.** Any attempt to express the value of the gold, silver, and bronze here listed, in terms of modern values, would fail to account for their true value at that time in purchasing power. A rough estimate of the total value, as determined by the weight of the three metals, would perhaps be more than 3 million dollars. Even critical scholars recognize that this detailed list of treasures and the list of family heads returning with Ezra bear the stamp of genuineness. If the book of Ezra were merely fiction, the author would hardly have devoted so much space to tedious lists of the returning exiles or have itemized the treasures.
Although a considerable portion of this treasure may have come from the royal purse, much of it was donated by the wealthy Jews of Persia and Babylonia, and some by their Gentile friends (see ch. 7:15, 16). While the amount of treasure carried back to Judea seems large, it should not be forgotten that the wealth of Persia at this time was immense (see Dan. 11:2). According to Herodotus (iii. 94, 95) India paid an annual tribute of 360 talents of gold dust (13.5 tons; 12.3 metric tons), Babylonia 1,000 talents of silver (37.7 tons; 34.3 metric tons), and large amounts were paid by other satrapies of the empire. The total revenues of the empire are given by Herodotus as 14,560 Euboeic talents. In comparison with this vast sum, the treasure carried to Judea by Ezra does not appear excessive, as some commentators have suggested.

27.zh:
金碗二十個，重一千達利克；上等光銅的器皿兩個，寶貴如金。

**上等光銅的器皿。**這個翻譯是準確的，但不知道是什麼樣的器皿，或為什麼“寶貴如金”。有人認為它們經過精密拋光，閃光如金子。還有人認為這是一種珍貴的銅汞合金。
27.en: **Vessels of fine copper.** The translation is correct, but it is not known what kind of vessels is meant or what it was that made these copper vessels “precious as gold.” Some have thought they were highly polished and glittered like gold, others, that it was the highly valued orichalcum, an amalgam of brass.

28.zh:
我對他們說：你們歸耶和華為聖，器皿也為聖；金銀是甘心獻給耶和華─你們列祖之神的。

祭司和利未人既已獻身歸於上帝，他們就是是聖物的合適保管人。
28.en: **Ye are holy.** Consecrated to God by their office, the priests and Levites were the proper custodians of consecrated things.

29.zh:
你們當警醒看守，直到你們在耶路撒冷耶和華殿的庫內，在祭司長和利未族長，並以色列的各族長面前過了秤。

**庫。**這些房間位於聖殿院子主要建築的兩側（見王上6:5）。有些給祭司居住，有些作為庫房（見尼13:5）。
29.en: **The chambers.** These rooms were on either side of the main building in the Temple court (see 1 Kings 6:5), partly as chambers for the priests, partly as storerooms (see Neh. 13:5).

31.zh:
正月十二日，我們從亞哈瓦河邊起行，要往耶路撒冷去。我們神的手保佑我們，救我們脫離仇敵和路上埋伏之人的手。

**十二日。**這個月初一，隊伍開始集合（拉7:9），但在指定聚集的地點三天的安營期間，以斯拉發現沒有祭司或利未人回應他的呼籲（拉8:15）。所以他採取了拉8:16—20所寫的措施，說服一些利未人和尼提寧人與他們同行。這些人來到以後，以斯拉就安排禁食，求上帝在路上保護，並把神聖的財寶交給祭司和利未人保管。這些準備工作化了八天時間，直到該月12日才從亞哈瓦河出發。
**埋伏。**以斯拉的擔心是有道理的。危險真的存在。但他對上帝保佑的信心得到了回報。我們不知道他們是如何從敵人手中得救的。但上帝自有祂的方式照顧那些獻身給祂的人並信靠祂的人。上帝親手帶領以斯拉和他的同行者經過路上的一切危險，毫髮無損地達到目的地。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第617頁。
31.en:
**The twelfth day.** On the first day of the month the company of travelers began to assemble (ch. 7:9), but during the three days’ encampment at the appointed place of meeting (ch. 8:15) Ezra discovered that no priests or Levites had responded to his appeal. Thereupon he took the measures described in ch. 8:16–20, to induce certain Levites and Nethinims to accompany them. Upon the arrival of these men Ezra ordained a fast to supplicate divine protection for the journey, and committed the sacred treasures to the care of the priests and Levites. Eight more days elapsed while these preparations for departure were being made, and the start from the river Ahava did not actually take place till the 12th day.
Such as lay in wait. Ezra’s fears were justified, and the dangers were real, but faith in divine protection was rewarded. We are not told how deliverance from their enemies was accomplished, but God in His own way took care of those who were consecrated to Him and who placed their trust in Him. The hand of God led Ezra and his fellow travelers safely through all the perils of the way, and brought them without loss or damage to their destination.

32.zh:
我們到了耶路撒冷，在那裡住了三日。

**我們到了耶路撒冷。**就像早年所羅巴伯領導下的迴歸一樣，聖經沒有記錄所經過的路線，以及長達四個月的跋涉經歷（《先知與君王》第617頁）。關於從巴比倫到猶大可能採取的路線，見拉2:68註釋。
**住了三日。**經過疲憊的旅程，需要一個短暫的全面休整。像尼希米一樣，以斯拉只要三天時間的休息。
32.en:
**We came to Jerusalem.** As in the earlier story of the return under Zerubbabel nothing is reported about the route taken or the experiences of the long journey of four months (PK 617). On the probable route from Babylonia to Judea, see on ch. 2:68.
Abode there three days. After the tiresome journey a brief period of complete rest was necessary. Like Nehemiah (Neh. 2:11), Ezra was content with a rest of three days.

33.zh:
第四日，在我們神的殿裡把金銀和器皿都秤了，交在祭司烏利亞的兒子米利末的手中。同著他有非尼哈的兒子以利亞撒，還有利未人耶書亞的兒子約撒拔和賓內的兒子挪亞底。

稱了。到第四天，以斯拉履行自己的職責，把從巴比倫帶來的各種禮物都交給了聖殿府庫。他當著管理聖殿的祭司和利未人的面，把第25-27節所列的金銀和器皿全部交給了他們。
**米利末。**他是祭司的領袖之一，歸以斯拉和尼希米所領導。在尼希米任省長時，他負責修復耶路撒冷的兩段城牆（尼3:4,21）。公元前444年，他是以斯拉和尼希米所主持代表以色列與上帝立約的簽約人之一（尼10:5）。
**以利亞撒。**和米利末一樣，是一名祭司。可能就是參加尼希米奉獻城牆典禮的那個以利亞撒（尼12:42）。
**約撒拔。**約撒拔和挪亞底是利未人的領袖。。約撒拔的名字還出現在拉10:23；尼8:7；和11:16中。
**懷愛倫註釋（33–36節）**。《先知與君王》第619頁                                   【 SDA3.1135】。
33.en:
**Weighed.** On the fourth day Ezra discharged his commission to present to the Temple treasury the various gifts from Babylonia. In doing so he appeared in person before the priests and Levites, who were in charge of the Temple, and transferred to them the entire offering of gold, silver, and vessels listed in vs. 25–27.
Meremoth. He was one of the heads of the priestly order, under both Ezra and Nehemiah. He is mentioned as repairing two sections of the wall of Jerusalem when Nehemiah was governor (Neh. 3:4, 21), and as one of those who signed the covenant between God and Israel that was later concluded under the guidance of Ezra and Nehemiah, in 444 .. (Neh. 10:5).
Eleazar. Being, like Meremoth, a priest, Eleazar is perhaps the individual of that name mentioned as taking part in the dedication of the wall in Nehemiah’s time (Neh. 12:42).
Jozabad. Jozabad and Noadiah were chief Levites. The former name occurs again in Ezra 10:23; Neh. 8:7; 11:16.

34.zh:
當時都點了數目，按著分量寫在冊上。

負責聖殿的祭司不僅清點和稱量了錠子和器皿，而且還造了冊，登記了每一個器皿的重量。這是為了防止保管人貪汙聖殿的財產，同時也卸下了以斯拉的責任，免得他以後遭人指控。在美索不達米亞，最小的交易也要有文字記錄。以斯拉無疑需要把收條送交王室檔案，證明諭旨的條款已經得到實行。
34.en: **The weight was written.** Not only were the ingots and vessels counted and weighed, but an inventory was made by the priests in charge of the Temple, and the weight of every vessel noted. Such was the care taken to prevent the embezzlement of Temple property by its custodians. It also relieved Ezra of further responsibility and protected him against possible later accusations. In Mesopotamia the smallest business transaction was documented, and Ezra was no doubt required to send back to the royal archives a signed receipt of delivery, as evidence that the provisions of the decree had been complied with.

35.zh:
從擄到之地歸回的人向以色列的神獻燔祭，就是為以色列眾人獻公牛十二隻，公綿羊九十六隻，綿羊羔七十七隻，又獻公山羊十二隻作贖罪祭，這都是向耶和華焚獻的。

正如所羅巴伯領導下的先輩在奉獻聖殿的典禮上為“以色列眾人”獻祭一樣（拉6:17），剛到達的迴歸者，作為全體以色列人的代表，顯然也為整個民族獻祭了。兩次所獻的祭牲是相同的。公山羊的數量一樣，但其他祭牲的數量上比以前少得多，因為隨以斯拉回來的人較少。除了綿羔羊以外，其他祭牲都可以除以12。不知為什麼用77只綿羔羊。也許像過去一些註釋家所說的是為了強調“七”這個數。
35.en: **Burnt offerings.** Like their predecessors under Zerubbabel, who had made an offering for “all Israel” at the dedication of the Temple (ch. 6:17), the newly arrived exiles, also apparently representatives of all Israel, offered for the whole nation. The classes of animals offered are the same on both occasions. The number of he-goats is identical, but in every other case the number of animals is far less than upon the former occasion. This is consistent with the comparatively small number of those who returned under Ezra. In each category the number, except for the lambs, was divisible by 12. The number 77 is difficult to explain, unless emphasis was thereby given to the number 7, as some of the older commentators have suggested.

36.zh:
他們將王的諭旨交給王所派的總督與河西的省長，他們就幫助百姓，又供給神殿裡所需用的。

**他們將王的諭旨交給。**主語從第一人稱變到第三人稱複數，不能證明作者變了（見拉7:28註釋）。這一節可能是歸納以斯拉結束了從東方到耶路撒冷的旅程。
**總督。**希伯來語是'achashdarpenim，與波斯語“總督”同義（見斯3:12註釋）。“河西的”總督駐在阿勒頗或大馬士革。很可能以斯拉的隊伍曾經停留在總督駐地，向他遞交了王室的授權書。到達耶路撒冷以後，以斯拉一定會將自己的任務告訴當地的省長，並向國庫的官員遞交了國王的撥款令（斯7:21,22）。以斯拉還會說他接受到所有這些官員們的合作。波斯人不大會與猶太人的利益作對。
36.en:
**They delivered.** The change in pronouns from the first to the third person plural is no evidence of difference in authorship (see on ch. 7:28). It is possible that this verse summarizes what Ezra had already done on his journey from the east to Jerusalem.
Lieutenants. Heb. ’achashdarpenim, the equivalent of the Persian term translated “satrap” (see on Esther 3:12). The satrap of “Beyond the River” had his seat at either Aleppo or Damascus, and it seems more than probable that Ezra’s caravan had stopped at the residence of the satrap and presented to him the royal authorization for his mission. After his arrival at Jerusalem Ezra must also have informed the local governor of his commission and delivered to the revenue officers the financial decree of the king (ch. 7:21, 22). Ezra adds that he received the cooperation of all these officials. The Persians are seldom found in opposition to Jewish interests.

1.zh:
這事做完了，眾首領來見我，說：以色列民和祭司並利未人，沒有離絕迦南人、赫人、比利洗人、耶布斯人、亞捫人、摩押人、埃及人、亞摩利人，仍效法這些國的民，行可憎的事。

**這事做完了。**以斯拉到達耶路撒冷已有一段時間了。他五月初一到達（拉7:9），休息了三天（拉8:32），五月四日向聖殿的管理機構移交了財寶，直到九月十七日才著手處理與異族通婚的事（拉10:8,9）。不能認為這件事引起以斯拉的注意以後，拖延了很長時間才行動。
**眾首領。**值得注意的是關於宗教違規的投訴是來自非神職人員，而不是耶路撒冷的宗教機構。這種不正常情況的原因是宗教領袖不僅容忍了這種做法，自己也違規了（第2節）。由於原先的大祭司耶書亞有近親娶了外邦女子，所以改革運動不可能由祭司們發起。宗教領袖自已都有牽連，難怪百姓會保持沉默。但在上帝善意的安排下，往往是神職人員腐敗了，就有自非神職人員起來發動宗教改革。
**效法這些國的民。**投訴中並沒有說猶太人已經接受了周圍異教徒的偶像崇拜，而是說他們與外邦鄰居聯姻。這些墮落的猶太人所娶的外邦妻子一定會把偶像的儀式帶進他們的家庭。
**迦南人。**提到猶太人與八個古代民族混雜，不一定是指娶了上述每一個民族的女子。赫人，耶布斯人以及亞摩利人，可能已不再作為獨立的民族存在。眾首領想到了《摩西五經》，如申7:1-4的禁令曾列舉了這些民族。他們提醒以斯拉，這些禁令已經被踐踏了。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–15節）**。《先知與君王》第619-621頁。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷一第279頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–2節）**。《先知與君王》第619頁。
1.en:
**When these things were done.** Some considerable time must have elapsed since Ezra’s arrival at Jerusalem. He had reached the city on the first day of the 5th month (ch. 7:9), rested 3 days (ch. 8:32), and on the 4th day of the same month had transferred the treasure to the Temple authorities. It was not till the 17th day of the 9th month that the matter of the mixed marriages was taken in hand (ch. 10:8, 9). We cannot suppose that action was long delayed after the matter came to Ezra’s attention.
The princes. It is remarkable that complaint on a matter of religious transgression came from the secular, not from the ecclesiastical, authorities of the city. The reason for this unusual situation is the fact that the religious dignitaries of the nation not only condoned the practice but were also guilty (v. 2). Since close relatives of Jeshua, the former high priest, had married foreign wives it is not strange to find that a movement for reform in this matter did not originate with the priests. When the religious leaders themselves were implicated it was understandable that the inferior orders should remain silent. By God’s good providence, however, it often happens that when things have come to such a pass, and the ministers are corrupt, lay people are raised up to take the initiative to secure religious reform.
According to their abominations. The complaint does not claim that the Jews had already adopted the idolatrous practices of the pagans about them, but that they were associating with these heathen neighbors. The foreign wives of these backslidden Jews had undoubtedly introduced idolatrous rites into their homes.
The Canaanites. Mention of eight nations of antiquity with whom admixture had taken place does not necessarily mean that wives had actually been taken from each of the eight groups listed. It is possible that the Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Amorites no longer even existed as distinct ethnic groups. The princes had in mind the prohibitions of the Pentateuch such as that of Deut. 7:1–4, where these nations are enumerated, and drew Ezra’s attention to the fact that these prohibitions had been violated.

2.zh:
因他們為自己和兒子娶了這些外邦女子為妻，以致聖潔的種類和這些國的民混雜；而且首領和官長在這事上為罪魁。

**聖潔的種類。**參賽6:13。不論以色列人多麼嚴重地犯罪汙染了自己，本著先知的預言和祂的恩典，他們依然是祂的子民，因為他們被拋棄的時候還沒有到。猶太人本是“祭司的國度，為聖潔的國民”（出19:6），“與地上的萬民有分別”（出33:16），是“屬上帝的子民”，即歸上帝所有的（見彼前2:9註釋）。
**在這事上為罪魁。**領袖們是罪魁（拉10:18）。在尼希米年代，領導階層中出現了相似的，甚至更嚴重的背道現象（尼6:17,18；13:4,28）。
2.en:
**The holy seed.** Compare Isa. 6:13. However much the people of Israel polluted themselves by transgression, they were still His people, by prophetic announcement and by His grace, since the time of their rejection had not yet arrived. The Jews had been ordained “a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation” (Ex. 19:6), “separated … from all the people that are upon the face of the earth” (Ex. 33:16), a “peculiar people,” that is, God’s own (see on 1 Peter 2:9).
Chief in this trespass. The leaders were the chief offenders (ch. 10:18). A similar, or even more serious, defection of the leading classes took place in Nehemiah’s time (Neh. 6:17, 18; 13:4, 28).

3.zh:
我一聽見這事，就撕裂衣服和外袍，拔了頭髮和鬍鬚，驚懼憂悶而坐。

撕裂衣服是東方人表示悲傷的一種常見方式（見創37:29,34；撒上4:12；撒下1:2；王下18:37；伯1:20；2:11,12；太26:65）。以斯拉是從巴比倫來的。那裡與外邦人通婚的現象可能並不嚴重。所以當他知道這種罪孽在迴歸者中發展到如此的程度時就十分驚訝。他用典型的東方人方式表達自己的心情，先撕裂外衣和內衣，再拔自己的頭髮和鬍鬚，最後坐下恐懼鬱悶，默不作聲，直到獻晚祭的時候。這種驚恐的表現是刻意要給他在屬靈上所領導的人留下深刻的印象。
**拔了頭髮。**這種做法聖經其他地方都沒有提到，但在次經裡有提到（次經《以斯帖》14:2等）。
**驚懼憂悶。**參但4:19；8:27。該詞表示相同的含義。漢譯為“心意驚惶”，“驚奇”。
**懷愛倫註釋（3–6節）**。《先知與君王》第620頁。
3.en:
**I rent my garment.** Rending the clothes was a common Oriental mode of expressing grief (see Gen. 37:29, 34; 1 Sam. 4:12; 2 Sam. 1:2; 2 Kings 18:37; Job 1:20; 2:11, 12; Matt. 26:65). In Babylon, whence Ezra came, marriages with pagans had probably not yet become customary. Ezra was therefore shocked when he learned the extent to which this sin had made inroads among the returned exiles. He expressed his feelings in typical Oriental fashion, by first rending both his outer and his inner garments, then tearing his hair and beard, and finally by sitting down astonished, motionless and speechless, until the time of the evening sacrifice. Such a manifestation of horror and amazement was well calculated to impress those whose spiritual leader he had become.
Plucked off the hair. This practice is not mentioned elsewhere in Scripture, though it is found in the Apocrypha (Apocryphal Esther 14:2; etc.).
Astonied. Compare Dan. 4:19; 8:27, where the same word is used in the same sense.

4.zh:
凡為以色列神言語戰兢的，都因這被擄歸回之人所犯的罪聚集到我這裡來。我就驚懼憂悶而坐，直到獻晚祭的時候。

**戰兢。**不但指對上帝的敬畏（見賽66:2），而且指因違法上帝的命令而害怕（拉10:3），以及因干犯律法而恐懼（申7:4）。
**晚祭。**在東方，早晨是從事業務的時間。我們可以推定首領們是在午前來見以斯拉的。獻晚祭大約在下午三點（見約瑟弗斯《上古史》xiv.4.3；又見出12:6註釋）。
4.en:
**Trembled.** Not so much a reference to God-fearing persons as such (see Isa. 66:2), but to all who were alarmed at the transgression of the commands of God (Ezra 10:3) and the threats of the law against transgressors (Deut. 7:4).
The evening sacrifice. As morning is the time for business in the East, we may assume that the princes had visited Ezra early in the day, certainly before noon. The evening sacrifice was offered approximately at three o’clock in the afternoon (see Josephus Antiquities xiv. 4. 3; see also on Ex. 12:6).

5.zh:
獻晚祭的時候我起來，心中愁苦，穿著撕裂的衣袍，雙膝跪下向耶和華─我的神舉手，

**我起來。**獻祭的時間也是禱告的時間，特別是認罪的禱告，和為整個民族的禱告。以斯拉可能認為在獻祭的時候，最適宜獻上懺悔和祈求寬恕的禱告。
**撕裂衣服。**以斯拉第二次撕裂自己的衣服，不僅再次表示他的傷心，而且無疑是要“聚集”到他周圍的百姓認識到形勢的嚴重性（第4節），從而促使他們悔改。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《善惡之爭》第178頁；《先知與君王》第48頁。
5.en:
**I arose up.** The time of sacrifice was also the appointed time for prayer, especially for a prayer in which a confession of sin was foremost or one of concern to the nation as a whole. Ezra probably felt that supplications for forgiveness would be most appropriate at the time when the sacrifice, which represented confession and forgiveness, was being offered.
Rent my garment. This second rending of his garments was not only a renewed indication of the depth of sorrow he felt, but also no doubt had the purpose of impressing the people who “were assembled” unto him (v. 4) with the seriousness of the situation, and to stir them up to repentance.

6.zh:
說：我的神啊，我抱愧蒙羞，不敢向我神仰面；因為我們的罪孽滅頂，我們的罪惡滔天。

**我抱愧蒙羞。**耶利米曾指責當時的人“行可憎的事……毫不羞愧，也不只羞恥”（耶6:15；8:12）。以斯拉可能想到這些話，就在他的禱告中向上帝表示他為百姓的罪孽而深感羞愧。
6.en: **I am ashamed.** Jeremiah had complained that in his days those who “committed abomination … were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush” (Jer. 6:15; 8:12). Ezra, possibly with these words in his thoughts, assures God in his prayer that he is deeply moved with shame for the sins of his people.

7.zh:
從我們列祖直到今日，我們的罪惡甚重；因我們的罪孽，我們和君王、祭司都交在外邦列王的手中，殺害、擄掠、搶奪、臉上蒙羞正如今日的光景。

**懷愛倫註釋（7–15節）**。《先知與君王》第621頁。

8.zh:
現在耶和華─我們的神暫且施恩與我們，給我們留些逃脫的人，使我們安穩如釘子釘在他的聖所，我們的神好光照我們的眼目，使我們在受轄制之中稍微復興。

**釘子。**路德，凱爾等註釋家認為這是指牆上的釘子（見賽22:23,25），上面可以掛用具，意思是上帝的子民得到釘子的支撐。其他人則認為這是帳篷的樁子，象徵著可靠的住所。
8.en: **A nail.** The nail, or peg, here mentioned has been taken by some commentators— Luther, Keil, and others—to be a nail in the wall (see Isa. 22:23, 25) on which utensils could be hung. The meaning would be that the people of God were sustained by this nail. Others have seen in it the tent peg, and thus symbolic of a sure abode.

9.zh:
我們是奴僕，然而在受轄制之中，我們的神仍沒有丟棄我們，在波斯王眼前向我們施恩，叫我們復興，能重建我們神的殿，修其毀壞之處，使我們在猶大和耶路撒冷有牆垣。

**波斯王。**以斯拉一方面哀嘆百姓的屬靈狀態，一方面感激波斯國王所給予的特權。實際上迄今為止每一個國王都對猶太人表示過眷愛。居魯斯第一個批准猶太人迴歸重建立聖殿（拉1章）；我們從厄勒番丁島的草紙文獻中得知，岡比西斯曾恩待在埃及的猶太人；大流士一世重申並補充了居魯斯的諭旨（拉6章）；亞達薛西一世現在頒發了新的諭旨，給予猶太人極大的恩惠（拉7章）。唯一的例外是偽斯麥爾地，在他當政的幾個月間曾妨礙過猶太人。
**重建我們上帝的殿。**見拉6:14；7:27註釋。
**使我們在猶大和耶路撒冷有牆垣。**《以斯拉記》第七章補充註釋已經指出，這句話不一定是指以斯拉到達耶路撒冷時城牆已經竣工。他是指波斯國王有關允許重建城牆的幾個諭旨。以斯拉作為奉命負責建造城牆的人，有權利說上帝“在波斯王眼前” 向他們施恩，使他們“在猶大和耶路撒冷有牆垣”。正如有些人所認為的，“牆”象徵著保護（見亞2:5）。
9.en:
**The kings of Persia.** While Ezra deplored the spiritual condition of the people, he is nevertheless grateful for the privileges granted by the Persian kings. Practically every monarch thus far had shown favor to the Jews. Cyrus had granted the first permit to return and build the Temple (Ezra 1), Cambyses had favored the Jews of Egypt, as we know from the Elephantine papyri, Darius I had renewed the decree of Cyrus (Ezra 6), Xerxes had granted unprecedented privileges to the Jews throughout the empire (Esther 8–10), and Artaxerxes I had now made new and far-reaching grants (Ezra 7). The only exception had been the false Smerdis, who actively hindered the Jews during the few months of his reign.
Set up the house. See on chs. 6:14; 7:27.
To give us a wall. It has already been pointed out in the Additional Note on ch. 7 that this statement does not necessarily mean that Ezra found a completed wall upon his arrival at Jerusalem. He refers to the several grants made by the Persian kings, particularly to permission to rebuild the wall. Ezra, who had been invested with authority to work on the wall, could therefore rightly say that God had extended mercy to them “in the sight of the kings of Persia, … to give us a wall in Judah and in Jerusalem.” Possibly, as some think, the “wall” is figurative and denotes protection (see Zech. 2:5).

11.zh:
就是你藉你僕人眾先知所吩咐的說：你們要去得為業之地是汙穢之地；因列國之民的汙穢和可憎的事，叫全地從這邊直到那邊滿了汙穢。

《舊約》中沒有這裡所引“眾先知”的話。所以要麼它來自得一位正典以外的受靈感作者，要麼是眾先知在這個問題上論述的歸納。引言的前半部分指摩西的時代（見申7:1-3）。《列王記》的作者對於“先知”（王下17:23；21:10；24:2）也有相似的說法。這樣引用是為了說明現在所探討的真理是人們經常談論的（見太2:23註釋）。
聖經其他地方（除了申7:1-3節之外）的確沒有如此明確地禁止與迦南人通婚。但是士3:6（在希伯來語的聖經裡，《士師記》被列為“前先知書”。見本書卷一第37頁）指責這種婚姻使猶太人受到誘惑去拜偶像。另外，在眾先知描述以色列人參與崇拜各地的巴力時，在他們譴責背道的時候，都明確包括這種違禁的行為。這就證明上帝不允許以色列人締結這種婚姻。以斯拉的這些話顯然不支持一些批評學者的觀點，即認為《申命記》“眾先知”所寫的。
**汙穢。**不是指身體的汙穢，而是寓指迦南各民族道德和宗教上的汙穢。關於迦南的宗教，見本書卷二38-41頁。
11.en:
**The land.** The quotation from “the prophets” does not appear elsewhere in the OT, and must therefore either be from a noncanonical, but inspired, writer, or a free quotation giving the consensus of prophetic teaching on the subject. The first part of the quotation refers to the Mosaic age (see Deut. 7:1–3). The author of the book of Kings makes similar references to “the prophets” (2 Kings 17:23; 21:10; 24:2). The purpose of such references is to represent the truth in question as one frequently mentioned (see on Matt. 2:23).
It is true that elsewhere in Scripture (except for Deut. 7:1–3) there is no specific prohibition of marriages with Canaanites as such, though in the remarks made in Judges 3:6 (in the Hebrew Bible Judges is counted among the “Former Prophets,” see Vol. I, p. 37) such marriages are reproved as occasioning the seduction of Israelites to idolatry. Also, in the prophetic descriptions of the whoredoms of Israel with the various local Baals, and in the general condemnations of apostasy, the transgression of this prohibition is implicitly included. This certainly justifies the general statement that God had forbidden the Israelites to contract such marriages. It is therefore evident that these words of Ezra do not support the argument of critical scholars that Deuteronomy had a number of “prophet” authors.
Filthiness. Not literal, of the body, but figurative, of the moral and religious filthiness of the nations of Canaan. On the Canaanite religion see Vol. II, pp. 38–41.

12.zh:
所以不可將你們的女兒嫁他們的兒子，也不可為你們的兒子娶他們的女兒，永不可求他們的平安和他們的利益，這樣你們就可以強盛，吃這地的美物，並遺留這地給你們的子孫永遠為業。

這條禁令採用申7:3的語氣。“永不可求他們的平安”與申23:6論到亞捫人和摩押人的話幾乎一樣。“這樣你們就可以強盛”回應申11:8。“吃這地的美物”的應許使人想起賽1:19。“遺留這地給你們的子孫”體現了好幾段聖經的意思（申11:9；箴10:27；結37:25）。
12.en: **Give not your daughters.** This prohibition is worded after Deut. 7:3. The addition, “nor seek their peace,” etc., is taken almost verbally from Deut. 23:6, in reference to the Ammonites and Moabites. “That ye may be strong” recalls Deut. 11:8, and the promise, “eat the good of the land,” suggests Isa. 1:19. The words “and leave it for an inheritance” embody the idea found in several Biblical passages (Deut. 11:9; Prov. 10:27; Eze. 37:25).

13.zh:
神啊，我們因自己的惡行和大罪，遭遇了這一切的事，並且你刑罰我們輕於我們罪所當得的，又給我們留下這些人。

**懷愛倫註釋（13–15節）**。《證言》卷一第279頁。

14.zh:
我們豈可再違揹你的命令，與這行可憎之事的民結親呢？若這樣行，你豈不向我們發怒，將我們滅絕，以致沒有一個剩下逃脫的人嗎？

以斯拉認為他的同胞已經“罪惡滔天”（第6節）。他們的罪等於完全背棄了上帝的誡命，所以他們在上帝面前無法“站立得住”（第15節）。以斯拉代表他的同胞公開認罪（見但9:5-16）部分是基於罪本身的性質，部分是因為他們忘恩負義，離開上帝。上帝饒恕了導致他們被擄的罪沒有不久。他們回到巴勒斯坦以後又一再蒙上帝施恩。以斯拉認為他們重蹈覆轍是罪不可赦的，其懲罰肯定是無可挽回的民族毀滅。
14.en: **Break thy commandments.** Ezra views the sin in which he found his people to have fallen as having “grown up unto the heavens” (v. 6). Their sin was tantamount to a complete forsaking of God’s commandments, and in this condition they “cannot stand” before God (v. 15). Ezra’s public confession on behalf of his people (see Dan. 9:5–16) is based partly on the nature of the sin itself, and partly on the fact that they had revealed base ingratitude in turning from God so soon after He had forgiven their sins that sent them into captivity and had showered favor after favor upon them as they returned to Palestine. To fall again into the same transgression was, in Ezra’s estimation, unpardonable, and the punishment must certainly be nothing less than irretrievable destruction of the nation.

15.zh:
耶和華─以色列的神啊，因你是公義的，我們這剩下的人才得逃脫，正如今日的光景。看哪，我們在你面前有罪惡，因此無人在你面前站立得住。

以斯拉代表他的同胞承認，上帝要求他們遵守祂律法的條款是本著祂的聖潔。與上帝的公義相比，他們的罪孽更顯醜陋可憎。
15.en: **Thou art righteous.** On behalf of his people, Ezra acknowledges the holiness of God in requiring them to comply with the provisions of His law. In contrast to His righteousness, their sinfulness stands forth in all its heinousness.

1.zh:
以斯拉禱告，認罪，哭泣，俯伏在神殿前的時候，有以色列中的男女孩童聚集到以斯拉那裡，成了大會，眾民無不痛哭。

**以斯拉。**接下來的部分，以斯拉退到幕後，使用第三人稱敘述。關於人稱代詞的改變，見拉7:28節註釋。
**成了大會。**許多人已來到聖殿參加每日的晚祭。當他們看到剛被任命為領袖以斯拉悲痛欲絕，承認百姓的罪時，自然深受感觸。以斯拉的真誠給他們流下了深刻的印象。他們全都哭了。以斯拉先是舉起雙手跪下禱告（拉9:5節），但不久他越來越感覺到百姓罪孽深重，就極其謙卑地撲倒在地。這種感人之舉動會讓東方的會眾深深動情的。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–5節）**。《先知與君王》第622頁。
1.en:
**When Ezra.** For the remainder of the narrative Ezra retires to the background, and speaks of himself in the third person. On the change of persons in pronouns, see on ch. 7:28.
A very great congregation. Many people had come to the Temple to attend the daily evening sacrifice. Seeing Ezra, the recently appointed leader, in the greatest imaginable distress, confessing the sins of the people, these men and women were naturally deeply affected. Ezra’s sincerity made such a strong impression on them that they all wept. At first Ezra had knelt in prayer with his hands uplifted (ch. 9:5), but soon, sensing more and more the heinousness of the people’s transgression, he threw himself upon the ground in an attitude of extreme humiliation. Emotional acts such as this could not fail to impress an Oriental congregation in the strongest way possible.

2.zh:
屬以攔的子孫、耶歇的兒子示迦尼對以斯拉說：我們在此地娶了外邦女子為妻，干犯了我們的神，然而以色列人還有指望。

**示迦尼。**可能是一個有影響力的人物，因為他在這裡似乎是作為百姓的代言人。雖然他的名字沒有列在娶外邦妻子的人當中，故不會被認為犯有這樣的罪，但他很難過，因為他的父親也屬於違規者。他的父親耶歇可能就是第26節所提到娶拜偶像妻子的人之一。他們都是以攔家族的人。示迦尼可能久已感覺到父親受外邦後妻的邪惡影響，所以衷心贊同以斯拉的話。他很高興這個問題引起以斯拉的注意。以斯拉一定和他一樣關注這種狀況。
**還有指望。**百姓痛哭流淚，表明他們的懺悔，所以有希望引導他們改正錯誤，歸向上帝。
2.en:
**Shechaniah.** Probably an influential man, for he appears here as spokesman for the people. Although his name does not appear among those who had foreign wives, and he must therefore be considered as having been free from this sin, he was deeply distressed by the fact that his father belonged to the transgressors, for it seems probable that his father, Jehiel, is the same person mentioned in v. 26 as among those who had married idolatrous wives. Both are of the family of Elam. Shechaniah may have long felt the evil influence of his father’s foreign (second) wife, and hence could honestly agree with all the words of Ezra. He seems to have been glad that the problem had come to Ezra’s attention, who was as much concerned about the situation as he had been.
There is hope. The penitence of the people, evidenced by their sore weeping, gave hope that they might be led to amend their ways and return to God.

3.zh:
現在當與我們的神立約，休這一切的妻，離絕他們所生的，照著我主和那因神命令戰兢之人所議定的，按律法而行。

示迦尼提出了具體的建議。他的建議說明他是經過深思熟慮的。以斯拉還沒有就這件事發表意見。示迦尼認為違法的婚姻不僅是錯誤的，也是無效的。摩西的律法允許在幾種情況下可以離婚（見申24:1-4；太19:3）。
**她們所生的。**小孩特別需要母親的照顧。母子分開將是十分殘忍的。此外，遺傳的傾向可能會使人養成背道的精神。大孩子也許已染上拜偶像的風習。至少示迦尼認為，最好的辦法就是讓孩子和母親一起離開。
**按律法而行。**這條建議的意思可能是指一，實施禁止這種婚姻的律法；二，依律法離婚（見申24:1）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《先知與君王》第623頁。
3.en:
**To put away all the wives.** Shechaniah came forward with concrete suggestions, which implies that this situation must have weighed heavily on his heart for some time. Ezra had not yet given advice in the matter. Shechaniah apparently considered marriages contracted contrary to the law not merely wrongful but actually invalid. The law of Moses permitted divorce for various reasons (see Deut. 24:1–4; Matt. 19:3).
Such as are born of them. Young children especially require a mother’s care, and it would have been extremely cruel to suggest a separation. Furthermore, hereditary tendencies were likely to perpetuate the spirit of apostasy. Older children might be already tainted with idolatry. It seemed best, at least to Shechaniah, to dismiss the children with the mothers.
According to the law. This suggestion may mean either: (1) let the law, which forbids these marriages, in this way be satisfied, or (2) let divorce take place as prescribed by the law (see Deut. 24:1).

4.zh:
你起來，這是你當辦的事，我們必幫助你，你當奮勉而行。

以斯拉的任務包括對不順從上帝律法的人實施審判（拉7:26），故理應採取行動。示迦尼保證“我們必幫助你”，這一定以斯拉很大的鼓勵。因為他知道自己在這件事上所採取的任何行動，都會受到許多違規者的反對。
4.en: **This matter belongeth unto thee.** Or, “it is your task” (RSV). Since Ezra’s commission included the responsibility of executing judgment on those who would not obey the law of God (ch. 7:26), Ezra was morally obligated to take action. Shechaniah’s assurance, “we are with you” (RSV), must have greatly encouraged Ezra, who realized that any action he might take in this matter would make him most unpopular with a considerable number of guilty men.

5.zh:
以斯拉便起來，使祭司長和利未人，並以色列眾人起誓說，必照這話去行；他們就起了誓。

以斯拉毫不猶豫，立刻行動。他通過宣誓把宗教領袖團結起來，實行他所完全贊同的示迦尼的建議。用宣誓來確認這樣重大的決定，符合《舊約》的做法（見書2:12；申6:13等）。
5.en: **Then arose Ezra.** Without hesitation he acted at once, binding the religious leaders by an oath to carry out the suggestion of Shechaniah, with which Ezra was in complete agreement. To confirm such an important decision with an oath was in harmony with OT usage (see Joshua 2:12; Deut. 6:13; etc.).

6.zh:
以斯拉從神殿前起來，進入以利亞實的兒子約哈難的屋裡，到了那裡不吃飯，也不喝水；因為被擄歸回之人所犯的罪，心裡悲傷。

**約哈難的屋。**關於聖殿的房間，見拉8:29註釋。關於約哈難，見拉七章補充註釋。這個約哈難似乎是尼希米時代的大祭司以利亞實的孫子（尼12:22,23；13:4,5）。厄勒番丁島的草紙文獻證明約哈難是公元前410年的大祭司。他既在聖殿裡有房間，就一定已超過二十歲（見拉3:8註釋）。有些註釋者認為本節的約哈難不是《尼希米記》和厄勒番丁島草紙文獻中的約哈難，但證據不足。
**不吃飯。**摩西曾兩次實行這種嚴格的禁食（出34:28；申9:18）。尼尼微的居民也有過類似的禁食（拿3:7），但只這並不普遍。禁食通常被理解為節制飲食（撒上1:7；撒下3:35）。有時禁食的人只須不吃“美味”，“酒肉”（但10:3）就行了。以斯拉的真誠表現在他禁食的嚴格上。百姓回應以後，以斯拉就到約哈難的房間裡哀傷。這表明他先前的激動是他真實憂慮的自然反應，而不像一些註釋家所認為的是精心策劃的表演。
6.en:
**The chamber of Johanan.** As to the Temple chambers, see on ch. 8:29. On Johanan, see Additional Note on ch. 7. This Johanan seems to have been the grandson of Eliashib (Neh. 12:22, 23), high priest in Nehemiah’s time (Neh. 13:4, 5). The Elephantine papyri attest that Johanan was high priest in 410 .. he already had a “chamber” in the Temple, and must therefore have been more than 20 years old at the time (see on Ezra 3:8). The objection of some commentators to identifying Johanan of this text with the one mentioned by Nehemiah and in the Elephantine papyri is not well founded.
He did eat no bread. Strict fasts of this kind were twice observed by Moses (Ex. 34:28; Deut. 9:18), and similarly by the inhabitants of Nineveh (Jonah 3:7), but they were not common. It was usually considered sufficient to abstain from eating (1 Sam. 1:7; 2 Sam. 3:35). Sometimes the person who fasted merely abstained from “pleasant bread,” “flesh,” and “wine” (Dan. 10:3). Ezra’s great earnestness appears in the severity of his fast. Ezra’s mourning in the office of Johanan, following the response of the people, clearly reveals that his previous emotional acts were the spontaneous expression of genuine horror, and not a well-planned theatrical performance, as some commentators have suggested.

7.zh:
他們通告猶大和耶路撒冷被擄歸回的人，叫他們在耶路撒冷聚集。

**被擄歸回的人。**以斯拉喜歡用這個詞組（見拉2:1；4:1；6:16,19；8:35等）。它包括猶大和以色列所有被擄歸回的人。
7.en: **All the children of the captivity.** A favorite expression with Ezra (see chs. 2:1; 4:1; 6:16, 19; 8:35; etc.), including all, from both Judah and Israel, who had returned from the captivity.

8.zh:
凡不遵首領和長老所議定、三日之內不來的，就必抄他的家，使他離開被擄歸回之人的會。

**三日之內。**當時的猶大大約北至伯特利，南至伯帕利（Beth-Pelet）和別是巴，東至耶利哥，西至奧諾（Ono）。所有的邊界離耶路撒冷都不超過80公里。故對於有活動能力的人來說，從聽到通告那天起至到達首都，三天時間足夠了。
**抄。**直譯為“奉獻”。這裡的抄家不是申13:13-17所描述的毀滅。那是針對拜偶像的城市的。而是將財產歸聖殿使用（見利27:28；見書6:17註釋）。
8.en:
**Within three days.** The limits of Judea at this time appear to have been Bethel in the north, Beth-Pelet and Beer-sheba in the south, Jericho in the east, and Ono in the west. As the frontier was nowhere much more than 50 mi. (80 km.) from Jerusalem, three days from the day that they heard the proclamation would allow sufficient time for all able-bodied men to reach the capital.
Forfeited. Literally, “devoted.” This forfeiture of property does not mean its destruction, as prescribed in Deut. 13:13–17 in the case of a city fallen into idolatry, but its appropriation to the sacred use of the Temple (see Lev. 27:28; see on Joshua 6:17).

9.zh:
於是，猶大和便雅憫眾人，三日之內都聚集在耶路撒冷。那日正是九月二十日，眾人都坐在神殿前的寬闊處；因這事，又因下大雨，就都戰兢。

**二十日。**公元前457年基斯流月二十日。可能是公曆12月7日（見本書第108頁）。
**寬闊處。**有文本為“大街”。可能指聖殿建築的外院，可以容納許多人。現在耶路撒冷的Haram esh-Sherîf，大致相當於古代聖殿的位置，連同其附屬建築，佔地約142,137平方米。其廣闊的院子裡可以容納幾千人。聖殿的狀況可能與此相似。
**戰兢。**人們從不出席所面臨的重罰，看出大會的嚴肅性。
**大雨。**這裡的九月，始於公曆十一月或十二月，給巴勒斯坦帶來了大雨。冬季的雨始於十月末或十一月初，為小陣雨，但到了十二月初，就下起了大雨。偶然提到“大雨”似乎並不重要，但證明作者是目擊證人，和故事的真實性。
9.en:
**The twentieth day.** In 457 .., Kislev 20 was probably Dec. 7 (see p. 108).
Street. Literally, “wide space.” This was probably the outer court of the large Temple compound. Great numbers of people could easily be accommodated there. The present Haram esh–Sherîf in Jerusalem, which corresponds roughly to the ancient Temple site, with all its auxiliary buildings, covers approximately 170,000 sq. yds. (142,137 sq. m.), and in its spacious, open courts many thousands of people can be accommodated. The situation with the Temple was probably similar.
Trembling. The seriousness of the reason for which the people had been summoned must have been evident to all from the heavy penalties with which they were threatened in case they failed to attend.
The great rain. The ninth month, beginning in our November or December, brings heavy rains to Palestine. The winter rains start toward the end of October or the beginning of November, with light showers, but by early December heavy rain is falling. The incidental mention of “the great rain” is one of those seemingly unimportant touches that mark the writer as an eyewitness and the story as authentic.

10.zh:
祭司以斯拉站起來，對他們說：你們有罪了；因你們娶了外邦的女子為妻，增添以色列人的罪惡。

此前，以斯拉似乎一直讓行政當局負責此事。現在他勇敢地站出來，斥責所犯的罪，並以最高領導的身份，命令與外邦妻子斷絕關係。
10.en: **Ezra the priest stood up.** Thus far Ezra seemed to let the civil authorities take the leading part in the matter. Now he came forward boldly, denouncing the sin committed, and, as supreme leader, commanded the repudiation of the strange wives.

13.zh:
只是百姓眾多，又逢大雨的時令，我們不能站在外頭，這也不是一兩天辦完的事，因我們在這事上犯了大罪；

“犯了大罪”的部分因素是違規人數之多。”
13.en: **We are many that have transgressed.** The marginal rendering of the KJV, followed also in the RSV, “we have greatly offended,” is a more exact rendering of the original text. Without doubt, however, the greatness of the offense consisted partly in the large number who had transgressed.

14.zh:
不如為全會眾派首領辦理。凡我們城邑中娶外邦女子為妻的，當按所定的日期，同著本城的長老和士師而來，直到辦完這事，神的烈怒就轉離我們了。

**不如為全會眾派首領辦理。**由於需要調查並處理的案件太多，故建議授權給行政和司法官員處理這件事。所有違規的人都必須接受他們的處置。
**直到辦完這事，上帝的烈怒。**這裡原文的語法有些模糊，但譯文可能是正確的。
14.en:
**Let now our rulers.** Since there were so many cases that would have to be investigated and settled, the suggestion was made that the administrative officers and judicial authorities should be authorized to deal with this matter, and that all those who had transgressed would be required to appear before them.
Until the fierce wrath. This clause and the remainder of the verse is grammatically somewhat obscure, but the rendering of the KJV and the RSV is probably correct.

15.zh:
惟有亞撒黑的兒子約拿單，特瓦的兒子雅哈謝阻擋（或譯：總辦）這事，並有米書蘭和利未人沙比太幫助他們。

**阻擋。**直譯是“站出來反對這事”。該詞在代上21:1；但8:25；11:14中也有相同的含義。
沒有說明約拿單，雅哈謝和他們的支持者反對的理由。這四個人也沒有列在違規者的名單中，所以不能說他們是想保護自己。第15節中的利未人米書蘭不是第29節的米書蘭。那人不是利未人。因為違規的利未人列在第23,24節。這四個人要麼是固執的狂熱分子，反對任何拖延，想要馬上解決問題，要麼是受人收買，為不敢公開反對的一些違規者說話。不管是什麼理由，他們都沒有成功。聖經記載，以斯拉所提出的措施得到了落實。
15.en:
**Employed about this matter.** Literally, “stood up against this matter,” meaning that they opposed it. The same words are used in this same sense in 1 Chron. 21:1; Dan. 8:25; 11:14.
The reason for the opposition of Jonathan, Jahaziah, and their supporters, is not stated. None of the four men is mentioned in the list of the transgressors, and no one could accuse them of seeking to protect themselves. The Levite Meshullam of v. 15 cannot be identified with the Meshullam of v. 29, who did not belong to the Levites, because the Levitic transgressors are mentioned in vs. 23, 24. These four men were either strongheaded fanatics, who opposed any delay and wanted the matter settled then and there, or they had been bribed to act on behalf of some transgressors who did not dare to voice their opposition publicly. Whatever their reasons, these men did not succeed. The narrative makes clear that the measures Ezra proposed were carried out.

16.zh:
被擄歸回的人如此而行。祭司以斯拉和些族長按著宗族都指名見派；在十月初一日，一同在座查辦這事，

**祭司以斯拉和些族長按著宗族都指名見派。**原文沒有說是誰進行了委派。有些註釋者和翻譯者把經文改成了調查小組是由以斯拉委派的。
**一同在座。**奉命處理個人案件的調查小組，從提別月一日，就是公元前457年十二月十八日開始工作。這是耶路撒冷的群眾大會決定將異邦妻子的問題提交由指定的領導人組成的調查小組處理十天以後。
16.en:
**Ezra … were separated.** The KJV faithfully renders the Hebrew text, which gives no indication as to who made the selection. Some commentators and translators alter the text so as to make it read that the commission was appointed by Ezra.
Sat down. The sittings of the commission appointed to decide individual cases began their work on Tebet 1, which was Dec. 18, 457 .., ten days after the mass meeting in Jerusalem had decided to refer the matter of the heathen wives to a panel of appointed leaders.

17.zh:
到正月初一日，才查清娶外邦女子的人數。

調查小組的工作到正月（尼散月）初一，即公元前456年4月15日結束。特別法庭的工作持續了幾乎四個月，因為在公元前456年春天，尼散月之前可能還插入了一個阿達爾月（見本書108頁；又見本書卷二103,116頁）。
17.en: **Made an end.** The work of the commission closed the first day of the first month, Nisan 1 of 456 .., which was April 15. Thus the sessions of the special court continued almost four months, because in the spring of 456 .. a second Adar was probably inserted before Nisan (see p. 108; also Vol. II, pp. 103, 116).

18.zh:
在祭司中查出娶外邦女子為妻的，就是耶書亞的子孫約薩達的兒子，和他弟兄瑪西雅、以利以謝、雅立、基大利；

**在祭司中。**以斯拉意識到國家有危險墜入他所設法除根的罪孽當中，就記錄了違規者的名字，以懲罰他們，並警戒他人。在違規者的名單裡，他首先列出責任最大的祭司。作為律法的監護人，他們有責任嚴格遵守律法的條例。按同樣的原則，在祭司以後列出了利未人。再列出了幾個違規的平民家族。在所羅巴伯名單的三十三個平民家族中只有九個違規。有一個家族在所羅巴伯的名單裡沒有。四個祭司家族中有三家，甚至有大祭司的近親，列入違規者中間。
**耶書亞的子孫。**在祭司中首先有四個人，是隨所羅巴伯回耶路撒冷的大祭司耶書亞的子孫和親屬（見拉7:1註釋）。
18.en:
**The sons of the priests.** Aware of the danger that the nation might relapse into the sin he was seeking to root out, Ezra punished the wrongdoers by placing their names on record, that others might take warning. First place in his catalogue of offenders he assigns to the priests, for their responsibility was greatest. As the special custodians of the law, they were obligated to adhere most strictly to its precepts. Next to the priests he lists the Levites, on the same principle. He then concludes with the laymen, arranged under their several families. The list of laymen suggests that only 9 of the 33 families mentioned in Zerubbabel’s list were involved. There is one additional family that does not appear in Zerubbabel’s list. Three of the four priestly families, on the other hand, and even near relatives of the high priest, were among the guilty.
The sons of Jeshua. First among the priests stand four names of sons and other relatives of the high priest Jeshua, who had returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel. As in many other places in the Bible, “son” here stands for “grandson,” or even “greatgrandson” (see on ch. 7:1).

19.zh:
他們便應許必休他們的妻。他們因有罪，就獻群中的一隻公綿羊贖罪。

這裡敘述耶書亞的親屬與他們的外邦妻子離婚的程序。他們首先以握手的方式──可能是與調查小組的成員──宣誓放棄他們的妻子，並使她們與以色列會眾分開。然後按照律法（利5:14-16；參利4:2）獻一頭公綿羊作為贖罪祭。以下的名單中只列出個人的名字和他們所屬的家族，沒有再重複離婚的程序。但對他們的要求是一樣的。
19.en: **Gave their hands.** Or, “pledged themselves” (RSV). The procedures followed with regard to the divorce of Jeshua’s relatives from their foreign wives are described here. First, they bound themselves by shaking hands—probably with the members of the commission—to put away their wives and to separate them from the congregation of Israel. Then they offered a ram as a trespass offering, according to the law (Lev. 5:14–16; cf. on Lev. 4:2). Throughout the remainder of the list only the names of the individuals and the families to which they belonged are given, without a repetition of the divorce procedure. It is evident from the context, however, that they were required to follow the same procedure.

20.zh:
音麥的子孫中，有哈拿尼、西巴第雅。

關於祭司的家族，見拉2:36-39。連大祭司的家族（第18節）在內，共提到有十七個家族違規。與《以斯拉記》第2章的名單相對照，可以看出隨所羅巴伯歸回的祭司中，沒有一等是不與這種違規有份的。第20-22節的有些名字還出現在尼8:4和尼10:2-9中，指的可能是同樣的人。
20.en: **The sons of Immer.** On the priestly families, see ch. 2:36–39. Including those of the high-priestly family (v. 18), altogether 17 priests are mentioned as guilty. A comparison of these names with those given in ch. 2 reveals the fact that not one of the legitimate orders of priests who returned with Zerubbabel was free from guilt in this matter. Some of the names given in vs. 20–22 reappear in the lists of Neh. 8:4 and Neh. 10:2–9, and may indicate the same individuals.

23.zh:
利未人中，有約撒拔、示每、基拉雅（基拉雅就是基利他），還有毘他希雅、猶大、以利以謝。

在利未人中只列出六個名字。但沒有說他們是屬於哪個家族。基拉雅，又名基利他，見於尼8:7和尼10:10。約撒撥還見於尼8:7。
23.en: **The Levites.** Of the Levites, only six names are given, and that without stating the houses to which they belonged. Kelaiah, better known as Kelita, appears under this latter name in Neh. 8:7 and Neh. 10:10. Jozabad appears again in Neh. 8:7.

24.zh:
歌唱的人中有以利亞實。守門的人中，有沙龍、提聯、烏利。

列出了一個歌唱的人和三個守門的人。
24.en: **The singers.** The names of one singer and three porters are given.

25.zh:
以色列人巴錄的子孫中，有拉米、耶西雅、瑪基雅、米雅民、以利亞撒、瑪基雅、比拿雅。

**以色列人。**即平民，共列出八十六個人。十個家族中有九個列在所羅巴伯的名單中。兩個巴尼家族（第29節和34節），在所羅巴伯的名單裡只有一個，說明第二家是以後回來的。
25.en: **Of Israel.** That is, of the laity, of which 86 names in all are listed. Of the ten families represented, nine are mentioned in the list of Zerubbabel. Since two families of Bani are given (vs. 29 and 34), and but one in Zerubbabel’s list, the second family of the two must have returned at a later time.

26.zh:
以攔的子孫中，有瑪他尼、撒迦利亞、耶歇、押底、耶利末、以利雅。

**耶歇。**可能是示迦尼的父親。他曾為以斯拉出主意（見第2節）。
26.en: **Jehiel.** Probably the father of the Shechaniah who counseled Ezra (see vs. 24).

44.zh:
這些人都娶了外邦女子為妻，其中也有生了兒女的。

這一節的希伯來原文有些含糊。中譯文十分接近於原文。大多數現代學者改動了原文，把後半節譯為：“他們送走了女人和她們的兒子”。無論原意如何，作者似乎都想說明，有了孩子離婚就更困難一些。所有案子的處理方式都是一樣的。
第18-43節的名單說明共有113個人娶了外邦女子。如果知道以斯拉時代猶大人口的規模，就能正確瞭解這種弊端在猶大的狀況。由於得不到這樣的數字，我們只能參照約八十年前隨所羅巴伯返回猶大的人口：

由於只有少數利未人隨所羅巴伯回來，與上列其他組別相比，他們違規的比例較高。其他組別在一千個人中平均至少有三人與外邦女人結婚。以斯拉在實施改革的措施時沒有遇到什麼反對，部分原因就是違規者的比例較低。
儘管違規的人數不多，其傾向卻是危險的。以斯拉和其他虔誠的領袖決心使國家擺脫異教的影響。與以斯拉的改革類似的做法在其他古代國家也發生過，目的通常是為了保持民族的純潔。公元前445年以前（有人說是公元前437年），羅馬是禁止貴族與平民結婚的。公元前451/450年，伯里克利曾在雅典實施一條法律：只有父母是正統雅典人者才能繼續作為雅典的公民。大約有五千人因為不是純粹雅典血統而不幸被賣為奴隸
以斯拉知道，公元前586年耶路撒冷毀滅、國家滅亡的大災難，是因拜偶像而造成的。必須千方百計防止這種罪惡死灰復燃。當他到達耶路撒冷的時候，這種罪惡還處在萌芽狀態。如果不加以制止，不久將無法控制。所以必須不惜任何個人代價予以根除。在大祭司和領袖的家族中也有人違規，這是特別危險的。以斯拉現在所採取，以及尼希米後來所採取的措施，使猶太人對於異族通婚產生厭惡。這種態度使猶太人一般不與外族通婚，直到如今。相比之下，猶大周圍的古代民族因為互相通婚和遷移，均已不復存在。
44.en:
**All these.** In Hebrew the entire verse is somewhat obscure. The most literal rendering would be the following, in which only two small grammatical adjustments are made in the Hebrew text: “All these had taken strange women, and there were some among the women who had given birth to sons.” Most modern scholars would alter the text and read the latter part of the verse thus: “and they sent away from them the women and their sons.” Whatever the original meaning, it seems clear that the author intended to convey the idea that it was more difficult to arrange a divorce where there were children than where there were not. All cases were dealt with in the same way.
The list given in vs. 18–43 shows that 113 men were guilty of marrying heathen wives. It would be interesting to know the size of the population of Judea in Ezra’s time, in order to secure a right picture of the extent of this evil in Judea. Since such figures are not available, a comparison can be made only with the people who had come to Judea with Zerubbabel about 80 years earlier.

Since so few Levites had returned in Zerubbabel’s time, the percentage of transgressors in this group seems high in comparison with the other groups listed. It is apparent that in all groups an average of at least 3 men in every 1,000 had married foreign women. The small percentage may explain, in part, why Ezra experienced little or no opposition to the reform measures he proposed to carry out.
Although the number of transgressors was relatively small, the tendency was dangerous, and Ezra, like other serious-minded leaders, was determined to keep the nation free from pagan influence. Parallels to Ezra’s reform occurred among other ancient nations, though usually with the purpose of keeping the race pure. In Rome patricians were prohibited from marrying plebeians before 445 .. (some say 437). In 451/50 .. Pericles enforced a law in Athens, according to which only those whose parents were full-blooded Athenians could remain Athenian citizens. Almost 5,000 persons were sold into slavery because they were so unfortunate as not to be of pure Athenian stock.
Ezra knew that the great disaster of 586 .., when Jerusalem was destroyed and the nation ceased to exist, had resulted from idolatry. A recurrence of those conditions must now be avoided by all means. The evil, still of small proportions when he reached Jerusalem, would, if unchecked, be out of hand in a short time. Therefore it had to be eradicated irrespective of individual hardships. The situation was especially dangerous because of the fact that leaders and members of the high-priestly family were among the transgressors. The measures of Ezra now, and of Nehemiah later, were instrumental in leading the Jews to look with abhorrence on mixed marriages, an attitude that has kept the Jewish nation comparatively free of intermarriage to the present day. In contrast, the ancient nations surrounding Judea have been lost through racial admixture and migration.

**一、卷名**
在希伯來文聖經中，《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》，原來合為一卷，直到1448年，希伯來文本才第一次依照武加大譯本的分法將其分為兩卷。這兩卷聖經原來合稱《以斯拉》，但在七十子譯本中它被分為兩卷，稱為《以斯拉記二》和《以斯拉記三》，前面還有《以斯拉記一》，裡面含有《以斯拉》和《尼希米》兩卷正典的節錄。哲羅姆首次將這兩卷正典命名為《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》，延續至今。他把七十士譯本中的《以斯拉記一》定名為《以斯拉記三》，將它列入《舊約》後典。
**二、作者**
《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》從歷史年代和文字上承襲了《歷代志》。研究其文體和語言可知它們與《歷代志》可能出自同一位作者。猶太傳統說法（見《塔木德》）稱以斯拉為主要作者，尼希米為編寫者。
雖然《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》不一定全部為以斯拉所著，但其中沒有什麼材料是不可能由他所寫的。作者採用了所羅巴伯和他自己那個時代的官方材料，還採用了可能由尼希米所寫的報導。在述及以斯拉和尼希米的工作時，有時採用第一人稱代詞，有時採用第三人稱單數，這不能證明有好幾位作者（有關以斯拉的第三人稱，見拉7:1-26；拉8:35,36；拉10:1-44；第一人稱見拉7:27-8:34；拉9:1-15。有關尼希米的第一人稱見尼1:1-7:73；尼12:27-13:31；第三人稱見尼8:1-12:26）。這種多樣性在古代聖經以外的其他文獻中也是存在的（見拉7:28註釋）。
出於尼希米12章中幾份祭司和利未人的名單延續到公元前400年左右（見尼12:10,11,22註釋），該書似乎寫於那個時代，也就是以斯拉和尼希米的時代。以斯拉是一位文士（拉7:6），很想讓百姓熟悉神聖的典籍（見尼8:1-8）。這樣的人很自然會作出安排，把發生在當代的奇妙大事準確地記錄下來，以指導和教育後代的人。我們完全有理由認為，以斯拉在聖靈的感動下寫了《歷代志》，《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》。在寫作過程中，他蒙聖靈引導對手頭的文字材料，如敕令（拉1:2-4；拉6:6-12等），信函（見拉4:11-16；拉5:7-17等）和名單（見拉2:1-67）等原始材料進行選擇。
《以斯拉記》中有兩段是用亞蘭文寫的（拉4:8-6:18；拉7:12-16）。過去有人據此認為《以斯拉記》的寫作年代要比以斯拉時代遲得多。這種看法在人們對波斯帝國時代亞蘭語分佈和使用情況知之甚少的時候，比較流行。後來不但在波斯帝國各地發現了許多亞蘭文文稿，在埃及也發現許多用亞蘭文寫的猶太人文稿，而這些文稿均出自以斯拉尼希米時代，於是上面這種看法就顯得沒有理由了。上述文稿中的亞蘭文與《以斯拉記》中的亞蘭文部分非常相似。當時亞蘭語已成為波斯帝國的官方語言，既用於通信和商業法律文件，也用於詔書法令。因此像以斯拉這樣有文化的人是通曉兩種語言的。在講話寫作時既能用母語，也能用亞蘭語。事實上，亞蘭語的使用已非常廣泛，任何有閱讀能力的人都懂亞蘭語。《以斯拉記》的作者當然也知道讀者能理解其中的亞蘭語部分，所以他覺得沒有必要把他所採用的原材料再譯成希伯來語。有關當時的亞蘭語文稿，見本卷註釋79-83頁。
**三、歷史背景**
除了《以斯帖記》以外，只有《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》是涉及被擄歸來後的史書，故對於研究歸來後猶太人的歷史是十分重要的。但是這兩卷書並沒有連續記錄上帝的子民在有關時期的歷史，而只記錄了其中的某些部分，尚有一些較大的空白沒有什麼資料可查。
《以斯拉記》首先記錄了猶太人在所羅巴伯的率領下從被擄之地歸回，重新開始獻祭的禮節，並開始建造聖殿。所有這些事大約都發生在居魯士（原譯為“古列”）作王最初兩年的時間裡。在以後的十三年裡，由於反對的勢力，工作進展緩慢。接著記錄了重新開始建造聖殿及至完工和奉獻。那是在大流士一世（原譯為“大利烏”）的統治下。關於以後的60年左右時間，以斯拉沒有記錄。然後到了公元前457年，以斯拉奉亞達薛西王的差遣回到猶大，擁有廣泛的權力，按照摩西的律法重建國家的行政機構。他寫到自己的回來和所開展的一些改革，但接下去又有十多年的空白，然後尼希米以省長的身份出現。《尼希米記》記載了他的活動。
《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》所載的所有事件均發生在波斯帝國曆史的前半葉。波斯帝國是從公元前539年巴比倫陷於居魯士勝利的軍隊開始，一直延續到公元前330年大流士三世去世為止，由亞歷山大大帝取而代之。被擄歸回後的猶大人歷史是從“波斯王居魯士元年”開始的（拉1:1）。波斯帝國東起伊朗沙漠，西至小亞細亞海岸，北起亞美尼亞高原，南至埃及邊界。帝國的創建者居魯士是一位謹慎而仁慈的君主。他的政策是讓巴比倫所奴役的各民族高興，所以他讓他們回到故鄉，恢復敬拜之所。根據這項寬厚的政策，猶太人被允許回到故鄉重建聖殿。波斯的各位君主大都設法公正而審慎地統治帝國。他們的官員受到告誡要處事誠實，為他們所管理的人民謀利益。至少從大流士一世起創立的國教──波斯拜火教，作為一神教，其水準要大大高於波斯以前巴比倫人的多神教和偶像崇拜。
居魯士攻取巴比倫以後認識了年邁的但以理。他是過去尼布甲尼撒王所信任的顧問。居魯士學會了尊重他的意見。他一定是通過但以理瞭解到以賽亞有關他以及他對於上帝子民所起作用的預言（賽44:21-45:13），於是他批准他們回國（《先知和君王》557頁）。居魯士的全付精力都放在安定初建之大帝國的重大工作。在消滅巴比倫以後大約九年，他在討伐悖逆的東方部族時喪命。
猶太人回到猶大以後，發現周圍的鄰居懷有敵意，又不斷受到在宗教和種族上均很混雜的撒瑪利亞人所騷擾。由於居魯士忙於統一他幅員遼闊的帝國，這些敵人成功地阻礙了猶太人，使他們苦不堪言，從而耽擱了重建聖殿的工作。
居魯士的長子岡比斯統治不到８年。他的最大功績就是征服埃及。從埃及發現的猶太文稿中可以得知岡比斯對猶太人很好。但沒有證據證明他實際幫助過猶太人建造聖殿。偽王斯默狄斯的短暫統治對猶太人十分不利。大流士說他是殿宇的破壞者。在他統治時，耶路撒冷的工作停了下來。停頓的部份原因可能是來自敵對的撒瑪利亞人。所以到了大流士一世的強大政府有較好的條件可以使聖殿再開工時，還得重新立根基。大流士大帝的時代是一個繁榮強盛的時代。猶太人和其他民族一樣，得益於他智慧和強大的統治。他們在先知哈該和撒迦利亞在屬靈上的領導下，於大流士6年，即公元前515年完成聖殿的建造，並舉行獻殿儀式。
但當大流士在晚年決定入侵希臘時，動盪的時代開始了。從那時起，波斯帝國在希臘和埃及等處屢遭挫折，影響了內部的和平和穩定。接下來的兩個王：薛西斯和亞達薛西軟弱，喜好投機，性格不穩定，大權落到有勢力的顧問手中。向希臘發起的災難性進軍，以及埃及等地的叛亂使帝國極不安定，導致內外政策的多變。
就在埃及發動嚴重叛亂的時候（公元前462-454年），以斯拉得到了國王給於猶太人的重大讓步。在這急難的時刻，亞達薛西需要猶太人的支持，因為猶大處在通往埃及的要衝。後來，當猶太人所屬的省區發生叛亂（公元450年以後），亞達薛西顯然支持他以為忠順的撒瑪利亞人。他錯誤地斷定並且擔心猶太人會參與叛亂，於是亞達薛西授權撒瑪利亞人阻止耶路撒冷城牆的重建。這時城牆已經造了一段時期了。後來省區的秩序得到恢復，王任命他所信任的宮廷官員尼希米繼任猶大地區省長。他在暴力的不斷威脅之下，完成了重建城牆的工作。
他當了兩任省長，證明是一位能幹的組織家和宗教領袖。他在政治，社會和道德方面奠定了比較穩定的基礎，對於以後動盪的時代具有重大的意義。
**四、主題**
《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》是史書，記載了上帝復興猶太人的計劃是如何得到實施的。他們又一次獲得機會與永恆的旨意相配合，爭取自己作為一個民族生存的權利。這份記錄還表明以賽亞和耶利米的預言是怎樣應驗的。它提供了極有價值的史料，使其他預言，如但以理第八章和第九章的預言，在歷史中有了可靠的依據。
《以斯拉記》和《尼希米記》通過一系列富有教育意義的事例，說明少數的人，在那些敬畏上帝，真誠無私，果斷無畏的領袖領導之下，能夠為上帝成就大事。這兩卷書能啟發和加強人對於上帝永無失誤之領導的信心。
